title: Godot 4.x and Web (glTF 2.0): glTF basics (presets `godot`, `web`, `gltf`)
text:
# Godot 4.x and Web (glTF 2.0)

## glTF basics (presets `godot`, `web`, `gltf`)
- `.glb` (binary, embedded textures) for delivery, `.gltf` + bin + images for debugging. Y-up, meters, right-handed. The exporter converts Blender Z-up automatically.
- Supported material: Principled BSDF → `pbrMetallicRoughness` (metallicRoughness texture: **G = roughness, B = metallic**; occlusion R via the "glTF Material Output" group → ORM in one texture), normal (OpenGL), emissive (+ `KHR_materials_emissive_strength`), alpha (OPAQUE/MASK/BLEND).
- Extensions the Blender exporter can write: `KHR_materials_transmission`, `_volume`, `_ior`, `_specular`, `_clearcoat`, `_sheen`, `_iridescence`, `_anisotropy`, `_dispersion`, `_emissive_strength`, `KHR_texture_transform`, `KHR_lights_punctual`, `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing`, `EXT_texture_webp`, `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `EXT/KHR_meshopt_compression`.
- Custom properties → glTF `extras` (`export_extras=True`), which Godot exposes as metadata.

title: Godot 4.x and Web (glTF 2.0): Godot 4 import
text:
## Godot 4 import
- Drop `.glb` (or `.blend`, if the Blender path is set in Godot's settings; it converts via glTF) into the project.
- Name suffixes on objects (Godot import hints): `-col` (mesh + static collision), `-colonly` (collision only, mesh removed), `-convcolonly` (convex), `-rigid` (RigidBody), `-navmesh`, `-noimp` (skip), `-loop`/`-cycle` on animation names (loop). Use them on Blender object names, e.g. `Crate-colonly`.
- Animations: each action → AnimationPlayer clip. Godot retargets humanoids via SkeletonProfileHumanoid (Bone Map in import dock).
- LOD: Godot auto-generates mesh LODs on import (`meshes/generate_lods`). No manual LODs needed.
- Lightmaps: enable "Light Baking: Static Lightmaps" on import to auto-unwrap UV2, or provide one.

title: Godot 4.x and Web (glTF 2.0): Web (three.js, Babylon.js, model-viewer, R3F)
text:
## Web (three.js, Babylon.js, model-viewer, R3F)
- Preset `web`: GLB + **meshopt** compression (`EXT_meshopt_compression`, or `KHR_meshopt_compression` via `--set export_meshopt_extension=KHR_meshopt_compression`) + **WebP** textures (q85). `--draco` switches to Draco (smaller for static, slower decode; needs the DRACOLoader).
- Budgets: hero model ≤ 2–5 MB GLB, total scene ≤ 10–20 MB, textures 1–2k, ≤ 50–100 draw calls on mobile web.
- Further compression outside Blender (recommended): `gltf-transform optimize in.glb out.glb --texture-compress ktx2` (KTX2/Basis textures: big GPU memory savings), `gltfpack -cc -tc` (the Blender exporter can call gltfpack: `export_use_gltfpack`).
- three.js: `GLTFLoader` + `MeshoptDecoder`/`DRACOLoader`/`KTX2Loader`. Set `renderer.outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` and tone mapping (`AgX`/`Neutral`) to match Blender's view transform (Khronos PBR Neutral ↔ `NeutralToneMapping`).
- Validate with the Khronos glTF Validator and view in https://gltf-viewer.donmccurdy.com or model-viewer.

title: Roblox (Creator Hub specs, verified 2026-10): Units and export
text:
# Roblox (Creator Hub specs, verified 2026-10)

## Units and export
- 1 stud ≈ 0.28 m. Default R15 character ≈ 5 studs tall.
- Blender FBX: **Apply Scalings = FBX Unit Scale**, every other scale 1.0, Path Mode **Copy** + **Embed Textures**, **Add Leaf Bones off**, Bake Animation **off** unless exporting a clip. That's preset `roblox`.
- Alternatives from the docs: Transform Scale 0.01, or scene Unit Scale 0.01 (the docs warn this causes Blender issues).
- glTF (`.gltf/.glb`) is supported and needs no scale tricks: preset `roblox_gltf`.
- The Roblox docs recommend Unit System None + Rotation Degrees in Blender to "match studs". Optional; keep Metric if you rely on the presets.
- **One animation per exported file.** Export each clip separately.

title: Roblox (Creator Hub specs, verified 2026-10): Mesh rules (all MeshParts)
text:
## Mesh rules (all MeshParts)
- ≤ **20,000 triangles per mesh**. Watertight, no holes/backfaces, no zero thickness, quads preferred, no n-gons.
- **One UV set**, all UVs inside 0–1 (overlaps allowed).
- Use `blender-asset-qa --profile roblox`.
- `RenderFidelity=Automatic` creates LODs, so don't ship LOD meshes. Set `CollisionFidelity` (Box/Hull/Default/PreciseConvexDecomposition) on simple parts.

## Textures / SurfaceAppearance
- Maps: `ColorMap` (RGB + alpha), `NormalMap` (**OpenGL, tangent space**, flat = 127,127,255), `MetalnessMap` (8-bit gray), `RoughnessMap` (8-bit gray), `EmissiveMaskContent` (8-bit gray) + `EmissiveTint`/`EmissiveStrength`. No packed ORM, so export separate grayscale maps.
- Max 4096²; PBR maps are commonly limited to 1024². Size guidance: 5×5 studs → 256², 10×10 → 512², 20×20 → 1024². Marketplace max 2048².
- `AlphaMode`: Overlay (default; alpha shows the part color), Transparency (cutout/blend), TintMask (alpha = where `Color` tints), Opaque.
- Files: PNG/JPG/TGA/BMP. Upload via Studio (`AssetService:CreateAssetAsync` for batch).

title: Roblox (Creator Hub specs, verified 2026-10): Rigging (any skinned mesh)
text:
## Rigging (any skinned mesh)
- Freeze bones: scale 1, rotation 0. Root bone at 0,0,0. ≤ **4 influences per vertex**, **no weights on Root**, symmetric weights.
- `blender-character-rigging` → `rig_check.py --profile roblox`.

## Avatar character bodies (R15)
- 15 meshes named `<Part>_Geo`: Head, UpperTorso, LowerTorso, Left/Right UpperArm, LowerArm, Hand, UpperLeg, LowerLeg, Foot. Each is watertight and capped at the joints.
- Facing **+Z, up +Y** in Roblox space (Blender preset conversion: front = -Y in Blender). Pose: I/A/T. Pivots at 0,0,0.
- Tri budgets: DynamicHead 4,000, Torso 1,750, each Arm/Leg 1,248, total **10,742**.
- Body scale (studs, X/Y/Z): min 1.35/3.6/0.7. Max Normal 8.6/9.5/2.25, Slender 6/9.5/2, Classic 8/9.1/2.
- Skeleton: `Root > HumanoidRootNode > LowerTorso > UpperTorso > (Head, arms)`, legs from LowerTorso. Root and LowerTorso at the origin. Up to 37 optional bones (Spine, Chest, Clavicles, fingers...) need `HumanoidRigDescription`.
- Attachments (empties) with `_Att` suffix: FaceCenter, FaceFront, Hat, Hair (head); Left/RightCollar, Neck, BodyBack, BodyFront (UpperTorso); Root (0,0,0), WaistFront/Back/Center (LowerTorso); Left/RightShoulder, Left/RightGrip; Left/RightFoot.
- Each body part needs an **outer cage** `<Part>_OuterCage`. Don't delete cage verts or change cage UVs.
- Marketplace: opaque body parts, ≥50% bounding-box fill, Material Plastic, VertexColor 1,1,1. Skin-tone areas transparent in the ColorMap.
- Dynamic heads: FACS poses as animation/shape data (see the Creator Hub "dynamic heads" page). Map ARKit-style shapes with `blender-facial-shapekeys`.

title: Roblox (Creator Hub specs, verified 2026-10): Accessories and layered clothing
text:
## Accessories and layered clothing
- Rigid accessories: ~4,000 tris max. Layered clothing: 4,000 tris max. Texture ≤ 1024² recommended.
- Layered clothing needs `<Name>_InnerCage` + `<Name>_OuterCage`, built from the Roblox template cages (same vert count/order/UVs as the template). The inner cage hugs the body, the outer cage hugs the clothing surface.
- Skin the clothing to the R15 rig (same bone names). Cages stay unskinned or follow the rig per template.
- Validate in Studio with the Accessory Fitting Tool.

title: Unity (2022 LTS / Unity 6): FBX settings (presets `unity`, `unity_skeletal`)
text:
# Unity (2022 LTS / Unity 6)

## FBX settings (presets `unity`, `unity_skeletal`)
- Apply Scalings **FBX All**, Forward **-Z**, Up **Y**. Static meshes: **Apply Transform** (`bake_space_transform=True`), which removes the -90° X rotation and the 100 scale on root objects. Never use it with armatures. Skeletal: Apply Transform off, and in Unity enable **Bake Axis Conversion** in the Model importer if the root shows a -90° X rotation.
- Smoothing: Face. Triangulate on (stable tangents). Leaf bones off. Deform bones only.
- Unity importer: Model tab Scale Factor 1, Convert Units on. Normals = Import, Tangents = Import (or Calculate Mikktspace).

title: Unity (2022 LTS / Unity 6): Humanoid (Mecanim) rigs
text:
## Humanoid (Mecanim) rigs
- Minimum 15 bones: Hips, Spine, Head, Upper/Lower legs, Feet, Upper/Lower arms, Hands. Chest, Neck, Shoulders, Toes, fingers and eyes are optional.
- Bind pose in **T-pose** (Unity can enforce it in Configure Avatar). Hips is the root of the deform hierarchy. An extra `root` bone above Hips is fine for root motion.
- Clean names (`.L/.R` map fine, or Rigify `DEF-*` after export with deform-only). Avoid twist bones parented out of chain; Unity ignores them for retargeting but they still skin.
- Root motion: animate the `root`/Hips; in the clip import settings, set Root Transform Rotation/Position "Based upon" Original/Body Orientation.

title: Unity (2022 LTS / Unity 6): Animation clips
text:
## Animation clips
- Export all actions in one FBX (`--set bake_anim_use_all_actions=true`) or one FBX per clip (`Hero@Run.fbx` naming lets Unity share the avatar). Loop: match first/last frames, set Loop Time in Unity.
- Blendshapes export as FBX shape keys (Model tab: Import BlendShapes; Blend Shape Normals: Calculate).

## Materials
- Unity doesn't build PBR materials from FBX usefully. Recreate them in Unity, or use extract + remap.
- URP Lit: BaseMap (sRGB), NormalMap (OpenGL), Metallic map: **R = Metallic, A = Smoothness** (smoothness = 1 − roughness). Occlusion separate.
- HDRP Lit: MaskMap **R = Metallic, G = AO, B = Detail mask, A = Smoothness**.
- Build the packed maps in Blender (`blender-texture-baking` → numpy channel pack) or in Unity with a packing tool.

title: Unity (2022 LTS / Unity 6): Other
text:
## Other
- Lightmap UV2: ship one (`uv_pack.py --lightmap`) or tick "Generate Lightmap UVs".
- LOD: name meshes `X_LOD0/1/2`. Unity auto-creates a LOD Group from the suffixes.
- glTF in Unity needs a package (glTFast). FBX remains the default.

title: Unreal Engine 5.x: FBX settings (presets `unreal`, `unreal_skeletal`)
text:
# Unreal Engine 5.x

## FBX settings (presets `unreal`, `unreal_skeletal`)
- Scene unit scale 1.0 (meters). Apply Scalings **FBX Units Scale**: the unit goes into the FBX header, so UE converts to cm **without** a 100× scale on the armature/root bone. A root bone that imports with scale 100 means the wrong apply-scale mode was used.
- Forward -Z / Up Y (UE converts the axis system). Smoothing **Face** (avoids the "no smoothing groups" warning). Triangulate on. Tangents on.
- Skeletal: **Add Leaf Bones off**, **Only Deform Bones on**, armature node type Null. If the armature object is named `Armature`, UE drops it and the first bone becomes the root. Otherwise the object becomes an extra root bone, so name the object `root` if you want that explicitly.
- UE 5.4+ also imports glTF/USD through Interchange. FBX remains the most battle-tested path for skeletal meshes.

title: Unreal Engine 5.x: Skeleton conventions
text:
## Skeleton conventions
- Mannequin (UE5 Manny/Quinn) hierarchy: `root > pelvis > spine_01..05 > neck_01..02 > head`, `clavicle_l/r > upperarm > lowerarm > hand`, `thigh > calf > foot > ball`, plus twist/IK bones. Matching the names and bone orientation lets the IK Retargeter auto-map them.
- The UE Mannequin's skeletal mesh faces **+Y** in its asset space (the Character Blueprint rotates the mesh -90° to face +X). After the first import, compare your mesh with the Mannequin in the Skeletal Mesh editor. If they differ, rotate the armature ±90° around Z in Blender, apply, and re-export, so retargeting and root motion line up.
- Bone orientation: Blender bones are Y-along. If you need UE-style X-along bones for engine-side tools, set `primary_bone_axis="X"`, `secondary_bone_axis="-Y"` with `--set`.

title: Unreal Engine 5.x: Static meshes
text:
## Static meshes
- Collision: `UCX_<MeshName>_00` (convex, ≤ 255 verts, not overlapping), `UBX_` boxes, `USP_` spheres, `UCP_` capsules, exported in the same FBX as the mesh.
- LODs: `<Mesh>_LOD0..N` in one FBX, with "Import Mesh LODs" enabled, or let UE auto-generate them.
- Lightmap UV: UE can generate one (Generate Lightmap UVs). Ship UV2 only for hand-made lightmaps.
- Sockets: empties named `SOCKET_<Name>` parented to the mesh.

## Nanite (static, UE 5.0+; skinned meshes experimental in 5.5+)
- Ship dense geometry directly (millions of tris). No LODs, no normal-map bake needed for geometric detail. Keep UV seams sensible (Nanite's error metric respects them).
- Opaque and masked materials are supported. Translucency isn't. Small/thin meshes (foliage) need care (Preserve Area option).
- Enable on import ("Build Nanite") or per asset.

title: Unreal Engine 5.x: Materials and textures
text:
## Materials and textures
- BaseColor (sRGB), Normal (**DirectX**: bake with `--directx`, or tick "Flip Green Channel" on the texture), **ORM** (R=AO, G=Roughness, B=Metallic; uncheck sRGB, compression Masks).
- Name textures `T_<Asset>_BC/_N/_ORM`. Materials become `M_` and instances `MI_`.

## Animation
- One action per clip. FBX exports the active action, NLA strips, or all actions (`bake_anim_use_all_actions`). Import the animation FBX against the existing Skeleton asset.
- Root motion: animate the `root` bone (not the armature object). Enable Root Motion on the anim sequence.
- Morph targets come from shape keys. Enable "Import Morph Targets".

title: Export Pipelines: One call
text:
# Export Pipelines

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Run `blender-asset-qa` (and `blender-game-optimization` for budgets) **before** exporting.

## One call
```
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset unreal_skeletal --objects SK_Hero --out //export/SK_Hero.fbx
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset web --collection Export --out //export/scene.glb
scripts/export_asset.py -- --preset unity --objects SM_A SM_B SM_C --batch --out //export/x.fbx   # one file each, at origin
```
Presets: `roblox`, `roblox_gltf`, `unity`, `unity_skeletal`, `unreal`, `unreal_skeletal`, `godot`, `web`, `gltf`, `usd`. Pass any exporter kwarg with `--set key=value`. Every preset is tested with a round-trip that keeps scale and avoids a 100× armature scale.

title: Export Pipelines: Engine reference (load only the one you need)
text:
## Engine reference (load only the one you need)
- [references/roblox.md](references/roblox.md): MeshParts, avatar bodies (R15), accessories, layered clothing cages, SurfaceAppearance, limits
- [references/unity.md](references/unity.md): FBX settings, Humanoid rigs, URP/HDRP maps, animation clips
- [references/unreal.md](references/unreal.md): static/skeletal FBX, root bone, collision UCX, LODs, Nanite, ORM/DirectX
- [references/godot-web.md](references/godot-web.md): glTF/GLB, import suffixes, three.js/Babylon, compression, KHR extensions

## Universal pre-export checklist
1. **Scale**: scene unit scale 1.0, objects at scale 1, rotation applied (except intentional object transforms). The presets handle unit conversion.
2. **Pivot/origin** where the engine expects it: props at the bottom-center, characters at the world origin between the feet, facing **-Y** (Blender front). Every preset converts that to the engine's forward.
3. **Modifiers**: the presets export the evaluated mesh. Mirror, bevel and weighted normals are kept; booleans become real geometry.
4. **Normals**: custom/weighted normals export. Smooth shading, plus hard edges marked sharp.
5. **Triangulation**: FBX presets triangulate (`use_triangles`) so the bake and engine tangents match. glTF always triangulates.
6. **Materials**: image-texture → Principled chains only, with names `M_*` and textures `T_*`. Procedural nodes don't export, so bake them first.
7. **Armature**: deform bones only, no leaf bones, rest pose = bind pose, 4 weights per vertex max, and the root at the origin.
8. **Animation**: one action per clip, named `Rig_Clip`. Bake constraints/IK to keys (`blender-animation`). FBX exports the active/NLA action per preset settings; glTF `ACTIONS` mode exports every action that has a slot for the armature.
9. **Naming**: unique, ASCII, no spaces. Engines key materials/meshes by name across reimports.

title: Export Pipelines: Format choice
text:
## Format choice
| Need | Format |
|---|---|
| Unity, Unreal (most stable for skeletal) | FBX |
| Godot, web, Roblox (supported), Unreal 5.x Interchange, Blender↔Blender | glTF 2.0 (`.glb`) |
| Film/VFX, Omniverse, Apple AR (`.usdz`), layout interchange | USD |
| Static geometry for printing/CAD | OBJ / STL (`wm.obj_export`, `wm.stl_export`) |
| Point caches / deforming sims | Alembic (`wm.alembic_export`) |

## Verify after export (required)
- The script returns `ok`, the file size, and for `.glb` a parsed summary (meshes, materials, images, animations, skins, tris, extensions). Compare it with what you expected.
- For FBX/USD: re-import into an empty scene (`import_scene.fbx` / `wm.usd_import`) and check `dimensions`, the armature scale (must be 1, not 100) and the action count.
- In the engine: scale against a reference (UE mannequin 180 cm, Unity capsule 2 m, Roblox character 5 studs), normals/smoothing, the normal map's green channel, and animation root motion.

title: Export Pipelines: Collection exporters (re-export in one click, 4.2+)
text:
## Collection exporters (re-export in one click, 4.2+)
See `blender-scene-setup`: `collection.exporters` stores the format + settings per collection, and `bpy.ops.wm.collection_export_all()` re-exports everything.

## Gotchas
- FBX `use_tspace` fails silently on n-gons. Triangulate first (the presets do).
- `bake_space_transform` (Apply Transform) is experimental. Use it for Unity static meshes only, never with armatures.
- glTF exports **actions** linked through slots/NLA. An action with no user on the armature is skipped (`export_animation_mode` options: `ACTIONS`, `ACTIVE_ACTIONS`, `NLA_TRACKS`, `SCENE`, `BROADCAST`).
- glTF needs image textures in PNG/JPEG/WebP. EXR/TIFF get converted (`export_image_format`).
- Linked library data exports fine, but make it local or override it if you need to modify it first.
- Shape keys: FBX exports them as blendshapes, glTF as morph targets (`export_morph`). Modifiers before the Armature modifier can block shape-key export in FBX (apply them first).

title: Facial Rig & Shape Keys: Choose the approach
text:
# Facial Rig & Shape Keys

The execution model is in `blender-core`. The body rig is in `blender-character-rigging`.

## Choose the approach
| Approach | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Blendshapes (ARKit 52)** | games, VTubers, mocap (iPhone/Live Link Face), web/VRM | the industry interchange set; each shape is sculpted |
| **Bones** (jaw, eyes, lids, brows, lips) | stylized, low memory, mobile | jaw + eyes as bones are almost always right |
| **Hybrid** | most production game heads | jaw/eye/tongue bones + blendshapes for everything soft |
| **Rigify face** (`human` metarig) | film-style keyframe animation inside Blender | 100+ face bones, heavy for engines |

title: Facial Rig & Shape Keys: Procedure (blendshapes)
text:
## Procedure (blendshapes)
1. The head mesh needs clean loops around the eyes and mouth (`blender-retopology-uv`), with eyes, teeth and tongue as separate objects parented or weighted to bones.
2. `scripts/shapekeys.py -- --mesh Head --create arkit` (or `--create visemes` for the 15 Oculus visemes) creates empty, correctly named keys.
3. Sculpt each key (live: sculpt mode on the active key, `use_shape_key_edit_mode`). Symmetric expressions can be sculpted once, then `--split eyeBlink` gives `eyeBlinkLeft/Right` with a soft blend across X=0 (`--falloff` m).
4. `--mirror browDownLeft` builds `browDownRight` (topology-independent mirror).
5. `--report` lists unsculpted keys, the max offset per key, and missing ARKit names. A shape is done only when every key moves and nothing is left over.
6. Optional: `--drivers FaceCtrl` adds a controller with 0–1 custom properties driving each key, for keyframing in Blender.
7. Check the extremes and **combinations** (jawOpen + mouthSmile, eyeBlink + eyeSquint) with `look`. Fix them with corrective combination keys driven by the product of two keys.

title: Facial Rig & Shape Keys: Shape key rules
text:
## Shape key rules
- Shapes are **deltas from Basis**. Never change the Basis topology after creating keys (adding or removing verts destroys every key).
- One action per key. No head or neck movement inside face keys (bones do that). Keep eyelids sliding over the eye surface, not through it (check with `blender-asset-qa` zfighting on lid/eye).
- Range 0–1. `slider_max` can be raised for exaggeration, but engines clamp to 0–1.
- Relative keys (`use_relative=True`, the default) are the only kind that exports.
- Name exactly per spec (case-sensitive): `eyeBlinkLeft`, not `EyeBlink_L`. Engines map by name.
- Keys on meshes with Subdivision: sculpt at level 0, and keep the subdivision modifier **after** the shape keys (they're evaluated first anyway).
- Applying modifiers on a mesh with shape keys fails. Use `modifier_apply_as_shapekey` for deform modifiers, or apply them before creating keys.

title: Facial Rig & Shape Keys: Correctives and combination shapes
text:
## Correctives and combination shapes
- Corrective for a bone pose: sculpt in the posed state, then drive with a `TRANSFORMS` variable (`ROT_X`, `LOCAL_SPACE`, mapped to 0–1).
- Combination: key `jawOpen_mouthSmile` with driver `SCRIPTED` expression `a*b`, from the two key values (`SINGLE_PROP` `key_blocks["jawOpen"].value`). Simple expressions don't need Python auto-run.

## Engine notes
- **Unity**: FBX blendshapes. In the Model importer, set Blend Shape Normals = Calculate (or Import if smoothing was exported). ARKit names map to the AR Foundation face-tracking samples.
- **Unreal**: morph targets ("Import Morph Targets"). Live Link Face / MetaHuman Animator use ARKit names, and the Pose Asset maps the curves. No leaf bones.
- **Roblox dynamic heads**: FACS-based poses with Roblox-specific names, authored as animation frames on a head rig (Creator Hub "Dynamic heads" spec). Build from the official Blender template. ARKit sculpts can be reused by renaming/mapping. Head ≤ 4,000 tris.
- **VRM / web (three-vrm, ReadyPlayerMe-style)**: ARKit 52 + visemes as glTF morph targets (`export_morph=True`). Keep the morph-normal export on only if shading needs it (it doubles the size).
- Drop unused keys before export. Every key costs memory per vertex (glTF sparse accessors help).

title: Facial Rig & Shape Keys: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- `ob.shape_key_add(from_mix=False)` copies the Basis. `from_mix=True` bakes the current mix (useful for combos, dangerous by accident).
- `shape_key_mirror(use_topology=False)` needs a mesh symmetric on X. Run it on the **active** key (the script handles this).
- Driver variables on shape keys use the Key ID (`ob.data.shape_keys`), not the mesh: `fc = kb.driver_add("value")`.

title: Game Optimization: Procedure
text:
# Game Optimization

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Always re-run `blender-asset-qa` after optimizing.

## Procedure
1. **Measure**: `scripts/mesh_stats.py -- --objects ... --budget mobile|roblox|web|vr|console|pc`. It returns tris, estimated draw calls, materials, texture VRAM, bones, and the over-budget items.
2. **Clean**: `make_lods.py --cleanup` (merge by distance 0.1 mm, dissolve degenerate, delete loose). Remove hidden faces: back-to-back faces and faces under other parts (`qa_check` → `back_to_back`, plus manual xray).
3. **Reduce in this order** (cheapest visual loss first): hidden/interior geometry → unnecessary edge loops on flat areas (Limited Dissolve 1–5°) → over-segmented cylinders → Decimate → bake detail to normals (`blender-texture-baking`).
4. **Materials**: merge to 1–2 per asset (atlas / trim sheet / shared tiling material). Each material slot per mesh is roughly one draw call.
5. **LODs**: `scripts/make_lods.py -- --objects SM_X --rename` creates `_LOD1.._LOD3` at 50/25/12.5%. Check every LOD silhouette with `look`/`review_shots`.
6. **Re-measure**, then QA, then export (`blender-export-pipelines`).

title: Game Optimization: Budgets (guidance per asset, 2026)
text:
## Budgets (guidance per asset, 2026)
| Platform | Hero char tris | Prop tris | Mats/asset | Max texture | Bones |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile | 5–15k | 0.3–3k | 1–2 | 1024 | ≤75 |
| Roblox | body ≤10,742 (head 4k, torso 1.75k, limb 1,248); accessory/clothing 4k | ≤20k per MeshPart | 1 (SurfaceAppearance) | 1024 (PBR), 4k max | R15 + optional |
| Web (three.js/Babylon) | 10–30k | 1–10k | 1–2 | 2048 | ≤100 |
| Standalone VR (Quest) | 10–40k | 1–10k | 1–3 | 2048 | ≤100 |
| Console / PC | 50–150k | 5–50k | 2–6 | 4096 | 150–300 |
| UE5 Nanite (static) | — | millions OK | few | 4096+ | n/a |
Whole-scene limits matter more than single assets: mobile ≈ 100–300k tris visible and < 100–200 draw calls; PC ≈ millions of tris and < 2–5k draw calls.

title: Game Optimization: Decimate modes
text:
## Decimate modes
| Mode | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `COLLAPSE` (ratio) | organic, scans, LODs | `use_symmetry`, vertex group factor to protect faces/hands; triangulates |
| `UNSUBDIV` (iterations) | meshes made by subdividing quads | restores the quad grid cleanly |
| `DISSOLVE` (planar, angle) | hard-surface / CAD | delimit `{"SEAM","SHARP","MATERIAL","UV"}`; keeps the silhouette, makes n-gons → triangulate on export |
Protect UV seams and silhouette: decimate a copy, then compare. If UVs tear at LOD1, the ratio is too aggressive for that topology, so re-unwrap or use a manual LOD.

## The hidden cost: vertex splits
GPU vertex count = unique (position, normal, UV, color) combinations. Every UV seam and hard edge **duplicates** vertices, so engine vertex counts are often 1.5–3× Blender's. Minimize seams where they aren't needed, keep hard edges = seams (so the split happens once), and don't add vertex colors or extra UV sets you don't use.

title: Game Optimization: LOD rules
text:
## LOD rules
- Halve the tris per level. Switch at screen size ~0.5 / 0.25 / 0.125 (UE "Screen Size", Unity LOD Group %, Godot `lod_bias` auto).
- LODs keep the same materials (or fewer: merge them at LOD2+), same pivot, same bounds.
- Skeletal LODs: remove finger/face bones at LOD2+ (the engine bone-reduction tools handle this). Keep the skinning on the same skeleton.
- Far LOD / foliage: impostor/billboard. Unreal Nanite (static, opaque/masked) and Godot's auto mesh LOD can replace a hand-made chain.
- Roblox: no manual LODs. `RenderFidelity=Automatic` does it. Keep each MeshPart ≤ 20k tris and use a simple `CollisionFidelity` (Box/Hull) for non-walkable parts.

title: Game Optimization: Draw calls and batching
text:
## Draw calls and batching
- **Merge** static meshes that share a material and are always seen together (join objects). **Don't merge** across large areas, because that defeats frustum/occlusion culling.
- **Instancing**: repeated objects as linked duplicates (Alt+D, shared mesh) or collection instances. They export as instances (glTF `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` with `export_gpu_instances`) or as one mesh + transforms in the engine.
- **Atlases/trim sheets**: put many props on one texture set. Trim sheets let walls, panels and pipes share one 2k material.
- **Texture memory** (upper bound, uncompressed RGBA8 + mips): 1k = 5.3 MB, 2k = 21 MB, 4k = 85 MB. Engines compress (BC7/ASTC ≈ 4–8×). Pack grayscale maps into ORM channels to cut it 3×.

title: Game Optimization: Collision
text:
## Collision
Keep collision separate and simple: boxes/convex hulls of ≤ 32–255 verts. UE `UCX_<Mesh>_##`, Godot `-colonly`/`-convcolonly` suffix, Unity MeshCollider on a simplified mesh, Roblox `CollisionFidelity`. Never use the render mesh as a physics mesh for anything that moves.

## Rig and animation cost
Limit to 4 influences per vertex (`vertex_group_limit_total(limit=4)` + normalize). Remove non-deforming bones from the export (`use_armature_deform_only`). Bake constraints and drivers to keys. Shape keys cost memory per vertex, so drop unused ones and keep only deltas (glTF sparse accessors handle this).

title: Game Optimization: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- Decimate on meshes with unapplied modifiers: `make_lods.py` evaluates them first. Other paths need you to apply them.
- Join (`Ctrl+J`) merges materials and UV maps by **name**. Rename the UV maps identically first, or the UVs get lost.
- The `Weld` modifier is the non-destructive merge by distance. Use `mode="CONNECTED"` to avoid welding separate parts.
- Triangulate before measuring if the engine will. Quads already count as 2 tris in the stats.

title: gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2): Scatter instances on a surface
text:
# gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2)

Pass these as `spec=` (MCP) or save them as JSON for `--spec`. Run `--describe` to check socket names when you change node types.

## Scatter instances on a surface
```json
{"name": "GN_Scatter",
 "inputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"], ["Density","FLOAT",10,{"min":0}], ["Seed","INT",0],
            ["Instance","OBJECT"], ["Scale Min","FLOAT",0.8], ["Scale Max","FLOAT",1.2]],
 "outputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"]],
 "nodes": {
   "dist": ["GeometryNodeDistributePointsOnFaces", {"distribute_method":"RANDOM"}],
   "obj":  ["GeometryNodeObjectInfo", {"transform_space":"RELATIVE"}],
   "rnd":  ["FunctionNodeRandomValue", {"data_type":"FLOAT"}],
   "inst": ["GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints"],
   "join": ["GeometryNodeJoinGeometry"]},
 "links": [["in.Geometry","dist.Mesh"], ["in.Density","dist.Density"], ["in.Seed","dist.Seed"],
           ["in.Instance","obj.Object"], ["dist.Points","inst.Points"], ["obj.Geometry","inst.Instance"],
           ["dist.Rotation","inst.Rotation"],
           ["in.Scale Min","rnd.Min"], ["in.Scale Max","rnd.Max"], ["in.Seed","rnd.Seed"], ["rnd.Value","inst.Scale"],
           ["inst.Instances","join.Geometry"], ["in.Geometry","join.Geometry"], ["join.Geometry","out.Geometry"]]}
```
5.2: Random Value has dynamic sockets (`Min`, `Max`, `ID`, `Seed` → `Value`) whose type follows `data_type`. Older tutorials use index-based duplicates, which no longer exist. Distribute Points outputs `Rotation` (aligned to the normal) directly.

title: gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2): Pipe / cable along a curve
text:
## Pipe / cable along a curve
```json
{"name": "GN_Pipe",
 "inputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"], ["Radius","FLOAT",0.05], ["Resolution","INT",12]],
 "outputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"]],
 "nodes": {"circle": ["GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle"],
           "c2m": ["GeometryNodeCurveToMesh", {}, {"Fill Caps": true}],
           "smooth": ["GeometryNodeSetShadeSmooth"]},
 "links": [["in.Resolution","circle.Resolution"], ["in.Radius","circle.Radius"],
           ["in.Geometry","c2m.Curve"], ["circle.Curve","c2m.Profile Curve"],
           ["c2m.Mesh","smooth.Geometry"], ["smooth.Geometry","out.Geometry"]]}
```
Apply to a curve object (`bpy.data.curves.new(..., "CURVE")`). Add `Resample Curve` for even segments.

title: gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2): Repeat zone (iterative subdivide)
text:
## Repeat zone (iterative subdivide)
```json
{"name": "GN_Repeat", "inputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"], ["Count","INT",3]], "outputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"]],
 "nodes": {"rin": ["GeometryNodeRepeatInput"], "rout": ["GeometryNodeRepeatOutput"],
           "sub": ["GeometryNodeSubdivideMesh", {}, {"Level": 1}]},
 "pairs": [["rin","rout"]],
 "links": [["in.Count","rin.Iterations"], ["in.Geometry","rin.Geometry"], ["rin.Geometry","sub.Mesh"],
           ["sub.Mesh","rout.Geometry"], ["rout.Geometry","out.Geometry"]]}
```
The repeat output starts with one `Geometry` item. Add more state with the 4th node field: `{"repeat_items": [["GEOMETRY","Geometry"], ["FLOAT","Value"]]}`.

title: gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2): Store a mask attribute for shaders/export
text:
## Store a mask attribute for shaders/export
```json
{"name": "GN_HeightMask", "inputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"]], "outputs": [["Geometry","GEOMETRY"]],
 "nodes": {"pos": ["GeometryNodeInputPosition"], "sep": ["ShaderNodeSeparateXYZ"],
           "store": ["GeometryNodeStoreNamedAttribute", {"data_type":"FLOAT","domain":"POINT"}, {"Name":"_height"}]},
 "links": [["in.Geometry","store.Geometry"], ["pos.Position","sep.Vector"], ["sep.Z","store.Value"],
           ["store.Geometry","out.Geometry"]]}
```
Read it in a material with an Attribute node (`attribute_name="_height"`). glTF exports `_`-prefixed attributes with `export_attributes=True`.

title: gn_builder recipes (specs verified on 5.2): Shader tree with the same builder
text:
## Shader tree with the same builder
```json
{"tree": "shader", "material": "M_Rust",
 "nodes": {"out": ["ShaderNodeOutputMaterial"], "bsdf": ["ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled"],
           "noise": ["ShaderNodeTexNoise", {}, {"Scale": 8.0}], "ramp": ["ShaderNodeValToRGB"]},
 "links": [["noise.Fac","ramp.Fac"], ["ramp.Color","bsdf.Base Color"], ["bsdf.BSDF","out.Surface"]]}
```

title: Geometry Nodes
text:
# Geometry Nodes

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Build trees with `scripts/gn_builder.py`, a compact JSON spec that's far cheaper than raw bpy. Look up exact socket names first, because they change between versions:
```
scripts/gn_builder.py -- --describe GeometryNodeDistributePointsOnFaces GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints
scripts/gn_builder.py -- --spec scatter.json --apply Ground --set Density=20 Seed=3 Mask=@paint_mask
```
`--set Name=@attr` feeds a modifier input from a named attribute. The result reports evaluated vert/face counts and node warnings. The spec format is in the script docstring; full examples are in [references/recipes.md](references/recipes.md).

title: Geometry Nodes: Core concepts (get these right or nothing works)
text:
## Core concepts (get these right or nothing works)
- **Geometry** flows left→right through sockets with **circle** shapes. **Fields** (diamond sockets) are functions evaluated per element **on the node that consumes them**, in that node's domain/context.
- **Domains**: Point, Edge, Face, Face Corner, Spline, Instance, Layer. `Capture Attribute` freezes a field at a point in the graph (before topology changes), and `Evaluate on Domain` converts between domains.
- **Attributes**: built-ins (`position`, `normal`, `sharp_face`, `material_index`, `UVMap`...) plus named ones via `Store Named Attribute`. Named attributes persist after the modifier. That's how GN data reaches shaders (Attribute node) and exporters (glTF `export_attributes`, which exports names starting with `_`).
- **Instances** are cheap (one mesh, many transforms). **Realize Instances** only when you must edit per-instance geometry or export a single mesh. Realize as late as possible.
- Inputs exposed on the group interface become **modifier inputs** (5.2: `mod.properties.inputs.<identifier>.value`). Panels group them, menu sockets give enums.

title: Geometry Nodes: Zones and advanced types
text:
## Zones and advanced types
| Feature | Nodes | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation zone | `GeometryNodeSimulationInput/Output` (paired) | per-frame state: growth, particles, erosion; bake to keep |
| Repeat zone | `GeometryNodeRepeatInput/Output` | iterate N times (L-systems, relaxation, recursive subdivision) |
| For Each Element | `GeometryNodeForeachGeometryElementInput/Output` | run a sub-graph per element (per building lot, per island) |
| Closures / Bundles (5.0+) | `NodeClosureInput/Output`, `NodeCombineBundle`/`NodeSeparateBundle`, Evaluate Closure | pass functions/structured data around; reusable "strategy" node groups |
| Lists (5.2) | `GeometryNodeFieldToList`, `ListGetItem`, `ListLength`, `SortList`, `FilterList` | real arrays, not fields |
| Grids/SDF (4.x–5.x) | `MeshToSDFGrid`, `SDFGridBoolean`, `SDFGridFillet`, `SDFGridOffset`, `GridToMesh` | smooth booleans, remeshing, fillets, voxel effects |
| Physics (5.2, experimental) | `GeometryNodeXPBDSolver` + bundles | node-based cloth/hair, see `blender-simulation` |
| Gizmos | `GizmoLinear/Dial/Transform` | viewport handles for inputs |
Zones need `input.pair_with_output(output)` (spec key `pairs`), plus items on the output node (`repeat_items`, `state_items`, ...; spec 4th node field).

title: Geometry Nodes: Procedure
text:
## Procedure
1. Sketch the data flow: source geometry → selection/masks (fields) → generate/instance → transform/randomize → realize/merge → set materials/shading → output.
2. `--describe` every node type you'll use, then write the spec and build. Check `node_warnings` and the evaluated counts.
3. Expose only meaningful inputs (density, seed, scale range, materials), with min/max set.
4. Look at it (`look`), check `blender-asset-qa` if the result will be exported (realized geometry), and check `blender-game-optimization` for instance counts and tris.
5. Ship: either keep it procedural (the .blend/asset library), or apply the modifier / `visual_geometry_to_objects` for exporters.

title: Geometry Nodes: Rules
text:
## Rules
- Randomness: always expose a `Seed`, and use `Random Value` with the ID/Index field so results stay stable when counts change.
- Scale-independent setups use `Object Info` (Relative) and real units. Apply the object scale or read it explicitly.
- Materials: `Set Material` inside the tree. The material must exist in the file, and instances keep their own materials.
- Shading: GN output loses auto-smooth unless you add `Set Shade Smooth` + (5.x) the `Smooth by Angle` essentials group, or store `sharp_edge`.
- UVs: primitives output `UVMap` via their UV output. Store it with `Store Named Attribute` (Face Corner, 2D Vector, name `UVMap`) or it's dropped.
- Performance: avoid realizing millions of instances, prefer Points + instances for scatter, use `Merge by Distance` sparingly, and simulation zones need baking for playback/export (`object.geometry_node_bake_single` or modifier `bakes`).
- Node tools (`ng.is_tool = True`, `is_mode_edit` etc.) turn a group into an operator in the 3D View menus, for editing workflows.

title: Geometry Nodes: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- 5.2: `mod["Socket_2"]` no longer works. Use `getattr(mod.properties.inputs, ident).value`, and `.type = "ATTRIBUTE"` + `.attribute_name` for attribute inputs. Compare and Random Value **sockets changed**: Random Value now has single dynamic `Min`/`Max`/`Value` sockets typed by `data_type`. Link by name, and `--describe` when unsure.
- Sockets that are disabled for the current mode/data type are still in `node.inputs` with the same name. The builder picks the **enabled** one. Set `data_type`/`mode` props first (the builder sets props before links).
- `nt.interface.new_socket(...)` is the 4.0+ API (`ng.inputs.new` is gone).
- Exporters see the **evaluated** mesh. Instances become glTF instancing (`export_gpu_instances`) or are realized on export.

title: Hard-Surface Modeling: Pick the workflow first
text:
# Hard-Surface Modeling

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Run `blender-asset-qa` after every modeling pass.

## Pick the workflow first
| Workflow | When | Output |
|---|---|---|
| **Mid-poly** (bevel + weighted normals, no bake) | modern games, props seen up close, fast iteration | game mesh directly; tiling materials/trim sheets |
| **High → low** (high via booleans+bevel or subd, low baked) | hero assets, unique textures, tight tri budgets | `_high` + `_low` → `blender-texture-baking` |
| **Subdivision** (support loops/creases + Subsurf) | renders, product viz, film | smooth surfaces, edges held by loops/creases |

title: Hard-Surface Modeling: Procedure
text:
## Procedure
1. **Blockout** at real scale (`ob.dimensions`) from primitives. Settle the silhouette and proportions before any detail. Check against references.
2. **Apply scale** (`transform_apply(scale=True)`) before bevels, booleans or solidify, because modifier distances use object space.
3. **Primary → secondary → tertiary** forms. Booleans for cuts and panels, then bevels. Small tertiary details go in normal maps/decals, or into the high-poly as "floaters" for baking.
4. **UV the base mesh now** (mid-poly). Bevel/Boolean modifiers propagate UVs, but after bevels no edge is sharp enough to auto-seam. Then **build the stack** with `scripts/apply_stack.py -- --objects Body --preset midpoly --cutters Cut1 Cut2`. Order: Mirror → Booleans → Bevel → Weighted Normal → (Triangulate at export).
5. **Shading check**: smooth shading + Weighted Normal (keep sharp). There must be no gradients across flat faces. View with a matcap or `look` in `solid` shading.
6. **QA** with `blender-asset-qa`, then apply the stack only on an export copy (`--apply`), keeping the editable source.

title: Hard-Surface Modeling: Stack rules
text:
## Stack rules
- **Booleans**: put cutters in a `Cutters` collection with display `WIRE` and `hide_render=True`. Solver: `EXACT` (robust default), `MANIFOLD` (much faster, but inputs must be closed manifold), `FLOAT` (legacy fast, fragile with coplanar faces). With many cutters, use `operand_type="COLLECTION"`.
- Avoid coplanar boolean faces: extend cutters slightly past the surface. They also cause z-fighting.
- **Bevel**: `limit_method="ANGLE"` (30°), or `"WEIGHT"` with a `bevel_weight_edge` attribute for hand-picked edges. Turn on `use_clamp_overlap`, `harden_normals=True`, `miter_outer="MITER_ARC"`. Width ≈ 0.5–2% of the part's size, kept consistent across the asset.
- **Weighted Normal** after Bevel: `mode="FACE_AREA"`, `keep_sharp=True`, weight 50. Needs smooth faces (remove the `sharp_face` attribute or call `shade_smooth`).
- **Smooth by Angle** (4.1+, replaces auto smooth): `bpy.ops.object.shade_auto_smooth(angle=rad)` adds a GN modifier, or `shade_smooth_by_angle` sets `sharp_edge` destructively.
- **Mirror**: `use_clip=True`, `use_mirror_merge=True`. Model one half only at x ≥ 0.
- **Subdivision**: hold edges with support loops (a loop 1–5% of the face width from the edge) or `crease_edge` (0–1). Turn on `use_limit_surface`. Don't use creases if the asset goes to an engine.
- **Triangulate** only for export/baking (`keep_custom_normals=True`, `BEAUTY`). Triangulating the bake mesh and the export mesh identically keeps normal maps synced.

title: Hard-Surface Modeling: Topology rules
text:
## Topology rules
- **N-gons**: fine on flat, non-deforming faces in mid-poly/game meshes. Never use them on curved surfaces or anything that subdivides or deforms.
- **Poles** (5+ edges) should sit on flat areas, never on a curvature peak or bevel.
- **Cylinder segments by on-screen size**: small (bolts) 6–8, medium (handles) 12–16, large (barrels) 24–32, hero/close-up 48+. Use multiples of 4 or 8 so booleans/mirrors line up with existing loops.
- **No long, thin triangles** across visible curved areas (shading and LOD artifacts).
- **Panel lines**: inset + extrude in (mid-poly) or a boolean groove on the high-poly, then bake.
- Spend density where the silhouette needs it, not on flat faces.

title: Hard-Surface Modeling: Edge/face attributes from Python (4.0+ names)
text:
## Edge/face attributes from Python (4.0+ names)
```python
me = ob.data
bw = me.attributes.get("bevel_weight_edge") or me.attributes.new("bevel_weight_edge", "FLOAT", "EDGE")
cr = me.attributes.get("crease_edge") or me.attributes.new("crease_edge", "FLOAT", "EDGE")
sh = me.attributes.get("sharp_edge") or me.attributes.new("sharp_edge", "BOOLEAN", "EDGE")
bw.data[edge_index].value = 1.0; sh.data[edge_index].value = True
me.edges[edge_index].use_seam = True          # seams are still an edge property
```
Select sharp edges by angle in bmesh: `e.calc_face_angle(0) > math.radians(30)`.

## Gotchas
- A bevel that looks blobby or flips usually means unapplied/non-uniform scale or overlapping geometry (turn on clamp).
- A Boolean that returns nothing or garbage: the cutter isn't closed/manifold (Exact copes, Manifold fails), or its normals are inverted.
- Weighted Normal has no effect: faces are flat-shaded, or an earlier modifier destroyed the custom normals.
- 5.2: the GN `Mesh Bevel` node exists for procedural bevels inside node trees (`blender-geometry-nodes`).
- Trim-sheet/mid-poly assets: UVs go to the trim strips (`blender-retopology-uv`) and materials tile (`blender-pbr-materials`).

title: Lighting & Look-dev: One call: presentation scene
text:
# Lighting & Look-dev

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Render settings are in `blender-rendering`. Full time-of-day, night and fog environments are in `blender-time-of-day`.

## One call: presentation scene
```
scripts/turntable.py -- --objects Hero --rig studio --backdrop --frames 120 --lens 85
scripts/turntable.py -- --objects Hero --rig both --hdri //hdri/studio_small_09_2k.exr --hdri-strength 0.8
```
This builds a camera framed to the bounding sphere (on the narrower frame axis), a key/fill/rim area-light rig scaled to the asset, an optional 18%-grey cyclorama, and a pivot that orbits camera + lights + backdrop in a seamless loop. **The asset itself isn't modified.** Everything lives in the `LD_Lookdev` collection, and re-running replaces it. Set the render resolution **before** running, because framing depends on the aspect ratio.

title: Lighting & Look-dev: Lighting recipes
text:
## Lighting recipes
| Situation | Setup |
|---|---|
| Asset / product review | 3-point: key 45° side, 30–40° up; fill opposite at ⅓ power and lower; rim behind for silhouette. Large soft area lights (size ≈ object), neutral grey backdrop, Khronos PBR Neutral view |
| Reflective product (metal, glass, car paint) | large softboxes/strip lights *reflected* in the surface, plus a black/white gradient environment. Shape the reflections, not the illumination |
| Exterior day | Sun light (angle 0.5° for sharp, 2–5° for softer) + sky (`ShaderNodeTexSky`, `sky_type` `MULTIPLE_SCATTERING`/`SINGLE_SCATTERING`; 5.x replaced "Nishita"; `PREETHAM`/`HOSEK_WILKIE` legacy) with `sun_elevation`/`sun_rotation` matching the Sun light, or an HDRI of the matching time of day |
| Interior | HDRI/sky through the windows + portal area lights in the openings, bounces ≥ 4, then practical lights (lamps) at real wattage |
| Character / portrait | soft key from above-front, a reflector-like fill, rim or hair light, an eye catchlight. 85–135 mm lens |
| Stylized / game screenshot | match the engine: one directional + ambient/HDRI, no fancy GI, so it looks like it will in-game |
- **HDRI**: Poly Haven (CC0) via the blender-mcp `search_assets`/`import_asset`, or `ShaderNodeTexEnvironment` + Mapping (Z rotation aligns the sun). Strength 0.5–1.5. Clamp sun hotspots if they cause fireflies.
- **Light linking** (4.0+, Cycles + EEVEE): set `light_obj.light_linking.receiver_collection` / `blocker_collection` (on the light **object**) to light only what you choose, like a hero rim that doesn't touch the backdrop. Portals: `light.cycles.is_portal = True` on area lights in window openings.
- **Units**: point/spot/area in Watts (a 60 W bulb ≈ point light 40–60 W in Blender), sun in W/m² (irradiance; 1000 ≈ physical midday, but use 3–10 with AgX for natural results), emission strength ≈ W/m². Keep lights physically plausible and control the overall image with exposure.
- **Shadows**: light size controls softness. A bigger, closer light is softer. Contact shadows should exist where objects touch, so check that nothing floats (`blender-asset-qa` `ground_z`).

title: Lighting & Look-dev: Camera rules
text:
## Camera rules
- Focal length: 24–35 mm environments/interiors (keep verticals straight: camera level, or shift instead of tilting), 50 mm natural, **85–135 mm products and portraits** (no distortion), 200 mm+ compressed telephoto.
- Composition: rule of thirds / centered symmetric for products, horizon off-center, leading lines, headroom. Show the silhouette (3/4 view at slight elevation 10–25°).
- DOF (`cam.data.dof.use_dof`, `focus_object`, `aperture_fstop`): f/2.8–5.6 for products at real scale. DOF depends on scale, so a wrong scene scale ruins it.
- Clip start/end tight around the subject (the script does this), which avoids precision artifacts.
- Sensor fit AUTO uses the larger axis. Portrait renders need framing on the width.

title: Lighting & Look-dev: Look-dev procedure (material approval)
text:
## Look-dev procedure (material approval)
1. Neutral setup: `--rig studio` or a neutral HDRI, grey backdrop, Khronos PBR Neutral or AgX (pick one and keep it).
2. Add a calibration chart object if needed (a grey 18% sphere, a chrome sphere, a Macbeth chart) next to the asset.
3. Turntable at 24–30 fps, 120–240 frames, 85 mm. Render previews with `render_batch.py --preset preview --format MP4`.
4. Check the materials under 2–3 different HDRIs. A good PBR material holds up in all of them (`blender-pbr-materials` sanity checks).

## Gotchas
- World lighting is invisible if `world.node_tree` has no Background → World Output link (the script ensures one).
- EEVEE needs `use_raytracing` for good reflections. Light probes (Volume/Sphere/Plane) still help static GI in interiors.
- Area lights that are too small and bright make fireflies in Cycles. Increase the size, decrease the power.
- A turntable that rotates the **asset** changes its transforms and animation data, which is why this rig orbits the camera instead.

title: Measured PBR values: Metals (base color = F0, metallic 1)
text:
# Measured PBR values

Linear values plug straight into socket `default_value`. sRGB values are for textures and color pickers.
Sources: Unreal Engine physically-based materials docs, physicallybased.info, DONTNOD charts.

## Metals (base color = F0, metallic 1)
| Metal | Linear RGB | sRGB 8-bit | Typical roughness |

| Silver | 0.972, 0.960, 0.915 | 252, 250, 245 | 0.1–0.3 |
| Aluminum | 0.913, 0.922, 0.924 | 245, 246, 246 | 0.2–0.5 |
| Gold | 1.000, 0.766, 0.336 | 255, 226, 155 | 0.1–0.35 |

| Brass | 0.910, 0.778, 0.423 | 244, 228, 173 | 0.2–0.4 |
| Iron / steel | 0.560, 0.570, 0.580 | 196, 199, 199 | 0.3–0.6 (brushed 0.25 + anisotropic) |
