title: Measured PBR values: Sanity checks for a texture set
text:
## Sanity checks for a texture set
- Average base color luminance for dielectrics: sRGB 50–200 (mean ~120). Pure black (0) or pure white (255) pixels on dielectrics are almost always wrong.
- Metal base color below sRGB 180: the metallic mask or albedo is wrong (it's probably dirt that should be dielectric).
- Roughness map near-uniform (std dev < 0.02): add variation.
- Normal map average ≈ (128, 128, 255). If the average blue is < 200 or the RGB is far off, the color space is wrong, or it's a height map labeled as normal.
- Check with `img.pixels.foreach_get(arr)` + numpy (`arr.reshape(-1,4)[:,:3].mean(0)`).

title: PBR Materials: Fast paths
text:
# PBR Materials

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Measured values are in [references/pbr-values.md](references/pbr-values.md).

## Fast paths
- Texture set → material: `scripts/build_pbr_material.py -- --name M_Crate --textures //tex/crate --objects SM_Crate`. It detects maps by filename (Poly Haven, ambientCG, Substance, UE suffixes), sets color spaces, splits ORM, flips DirectX normals, and routes AO to glTF.
- Solid physically-plausible material: `--preset gold|iron|plastic|rubber|wood|glass|skin|...` with an optional `--color R G B` (sRGB).

## The rules (violations are what make renders look "CG")
1. **Metallic is binary**: 0 (dielectric) or 1 (raw metal). Use in-between values only on transition pixels (dust or rust edges on metal). Painted metal counts as dielectric.
2. **Base color = albedo with no lighting**: no baked shadows/AO/highlights. Dielectric range is sRGB ~30–240 (linear 0.012–0.87): charcoal ≈ 50, fresh snow ≈ 240. Metals: base color = F0 reflectance, sRGB 180–255, never dark.
3. **Roughness carries the realism**. Break it up with grunge, smudges and wear. A constant roughness value looks fake; vary it ±0.1–0.2 across a surface.
4. **Color spaces**: Base Color and Emission use `sRGB`. Roughness, Metallic, Normal, AO, Height, Opacity and ORM use `Non-Color`. A wrong color space is the #1 bug (washed-out normals, wrong roughness).
5. **Specular**: leave `IOR` 1.5 and `Specular IOR Level` 0.5 for almost all dielectrics. Change IOR only for known materials (water 1.33, glass 1.5, diamond 2.42).
6. **Normal maps**: Blender, glTF, Unity and Roblox use **OpenGL** (Y+). Unreal and Substance's DirectX preset use **DirectX** (Y-), so flip G when converting. The bake and the target must use the same tangent basis (MikkTSpace) and the same triangulation.
7. **AO**: the Principled BSDF has no AO input. For engines, ship AO in the ORM red channel. For Cycles renders, don't multiply AO into base color, because the renderer computes occlusion.

title: PBR Materials: Principled BSDF (5.2) quick map
text:
## Principled BSDF (5.2) quick map
`Base Color`, `Metallic`, `Roughness`, `IOR`, `Alpha`, `Normal`, `Thin Wall` (5.2: leaves/paper/fabric sheets without volume), `Subsurface Weight/Radius/Scale` (skin, wax; Scale in meters ≈ 0.005–0.02 for skin), `Specular IOR Level`, `Specular Tint`, `Anisotropic`, `Transmission Weight` (glass/liquids), `Coat Weight/Roughness/Normal` (car paint, varnish), `Sheen Weight` (cloth, velvet), `Emission Color/Strength` (strength in W/m²-ish units; 1–10 for screens, 50+ for bulbs), `Thin Film Thickness/IOR` (soap, oil, coated lenses), `Diffuse Roughness`.

## Engine export rules
| Target | Maps | Packing | Normal |
|---|---|---|---|
| glTF / web / Godot | baseColor(+alpha), metallicRoughness, normal, occlusion, emissive | glTF: **R=AO G=Rough B=Metal** (ORM) | OpenGL |
| Unreal | BaseColor, Normal, ORM | R=AO G=Rough B=Metal | DirectX (UE flips on import if the texture is marked) |
| Unity URP/HDRP | BaseMap, Normal, MetallicSmoothness / HDRP MaskMap | URP: R=Metal A=**Smoothness** (1-rough). HDRP Mask: R=Metal G=AO B=DetailMask A=Smoothness | OpenGL |
| Roblox SurfaceAppearance | ColorMap(+alpha), NormalMap, MetalnessMap, RoughnessMap, EmissiveMaskContent | separate grayscale maps, no packing | OpenGL, tangent space |
- Only image-texture → BSDF chains export. Procedural nodes, Mix nodes and math become nothing in engines, so bake them first (`blender-texture-baking`).
- One material per texture set. Every extra material is an extra draw call (`blender-game-optimization`).
- Power-of-two textures (512/1024/2048/4096). Use PNG/TGA for data maps, never JPEG for normals.

title: PBR Materials: Alpha
text:
## Alpha
`mat.surface_render_method = "DITHERED"` (cutout/alpha-clip, sorts correctly, good for foliage/hair cards) or `"BLENDED"` (true transparency, glass/UI). Connect `Alpha`. glTF exports CLIP/BLEND from the alpha setup. Prefer dithered/clip for games.

## Displacement
Height map → `Displacement` node → Material Output `Displacement`. `mat.displacement_method`: `BUMP` (shading only, everywhere), `BOTH`/`DISPLACEMENT` (Cycles, needs dense or adaptively subdivided geometry: Subdivision modifier `use_adaptive_subdivision`). Scale is in meters; midlevel 0.5 for 8-bit, 0 for 32-bit EXR.

## View transform (judge materials under the right one)
`scene.view_settings.view_transform`: **AgX** (default, photographic), **Khronos PBR Neutral** (what-you-see-is-the-albedo; use for asset/product review and glTF parity), **Standard** (UI/graphics/textures that must match pixels), ACES 1.3/2.0 (VFX pipelines). Never bake or author textures while looking through Filmic/AgX with an extreme "Look".

title: PBR Materials: Procedural → texture
text:
## Procedural → texture
Procedural setups (noise/voronoi wear, curvature masks via `Geometry > Pointiness` (Cycles) or `Ambient Occlusion` node, edge wear via `Bevel` node normals) are fine for renders. For engines, bake them to the texture set (`blender-texture-baking`). Node Wrangler (bundled) `Ctrl+Shift+T` does the same as `build_pbr_material.py`, but needs the UI.

## Gotchas
- `material.use_nodes` is deprecated in 5.x. New materials already have Principled + Output.
- `mat.diffuse_color` only affects the viewport (Solid mode/workbench), not renders or export.
- Images loaded headless need `image.colorspace_settings.name` set **before** baking or export.
- Shared texture images used by several materials: change the color space once, because it's per image.

title: Pipeline Automation: Batch one-liners
text:
# Pipeline Automation

The execution model is in `blender-core` (`run_in_blender.py` finds Blender and prints only the JSON results).

## Batch one-liners
```
blender -b -P scripts/batch_process.py -- --in "assets/**/*.fbx" --op convert --to glb --out export/
blender -b -P scripts/batch_process.py -- --in library/ --op report                      # inventory JSON lines
blender -b -P scripts/batch_process.py -- --in "src/*.blend" --op script \
    --script ../blender-asset-qa/scripts/qa_check.py --kwargs '{"profile":"game"}'       # QA a whole library
blender -b -P scripts/batch_process.py -- --in src/ --op script --script ../blender-game-optimization/scripts/make_lods.py \
    --kwargs '{"rename":true}' --save-to processed/                                      # LODs for every file
```
Each file is streamed as one JSON line with `ok`, timing and results. Failures don't stop the batch, and the summary lists them. **Parallel**: start N processes with `--shard 0/N` … `--shard N-1/N` (Blender uses one core for Python, so processes scale with CPU/GPU count).

title: Pipeline Automation: Headless CLI essentials
text:
## Headless CLI essentials
| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-b` | background, no UI. Put it **first** |
| `file.blend` | open before running scripts. Order matters: args run left to right |
| `-P script.py` / `--python-expr "..."` | run Python |
| `--python-exit-code 1` | non-zero exit if the script raises (CI) |
| `--factory-startup` | ignore user prefs/add-ons (reproducible). Bundled add-ons still load |
| `--addons rigify,io_scene_fbx` | enable specific add-ons |
| `-E CYCLES -o //out/#### -F PNG -s 1 -e 10 -a` / `-f 5` | render (`blender-rendering`) |
| `--command extension build/validate/install-file` | extension tooling (`blender-addon-development`) |
| `-- --my args` | everything after `--` goes to the script (`sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--")+1:]`) |
| `--log "*"`, `--debug-python` | debugging. 5.0 changed the log format, so don't regex progress lines |
Environment variables: `BLENDER_USER_SCRIPTS`, `BLENDER_USER_EXTENSIONS`, `BLENDER_SYSTEM_PYTHON`. Use `OCIO` for custom color configs.

title: Pipeline Automation: bpy as a Python module
text:
## bpy as a Python module
`pip install bpy==5.2.*` (Python 3.13, matching the Blender release) gives `import bpy` in plain Python, which is handy for pytest/CI/web services. It has no UI and no GPU module by default, and it's large (~300 MB). Version-lock it with the Blender you target. The `bpy` wheel and the CLI behave the same for data API work.

## Library patterns
- **Append/link**: `bpy.data.libraries.load(path, link=...)` (see `blender-core/references/bpy-patterns.md`). 5.2: `data_from.libraries` exposes nested library paths when loading.
- **Write a subset**: `bpy.data.libraries.write(path, {datablocks}, fake_user=True, path_remap="RELATIVE_ALL")` builds asset/library files from a session.
- **Find files**: `bpy.data.file_path_foreach(...)` (5.2 flags: `EXPAND_TOKENS` for UDIMs, `EXPAND_SEQUENCES`, `EXPAND_CACHES`), and `bpy.utils.blend_paths(absolute=True)` lists every external path.
- **Remap/relocate**: `bpy.ops.file.find_missing_files(directory=...)`, `make_paths_relative`, `pack_all`. Libraries: `lib.filepath = new; lib.reload()`.
- **Iterate every ID**: `bpy.data.all_ids` (5.2), and `bpy.data.orphans_purge(do_recursive=True)` for cleanup.

title: Pipeline Automation: Robustness rules
text:
## Robustness rules
- One task per process where possible. Long Blender sessions leak (images, undo). `batch_process.py` reuses the process but resets with `read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)` / `open_mainfile`.
- Never write into the source folder by default. Use separate `--out`/`--save-to`, and write with `copy=True`.
- Make scripts idempotent: re-running replaces their own outputs (named prefixes, `exist_ok`).
- Log JSON, not prose: one object per file/job, so agents and CI can parse it cheaply.
- Pin the Blender version (5.2 LTS) for a project. Record `bpy.app.version_string` + hash (`bpy.app.build_hash`) in the outputs.
- Paths: `bpy.path.abspath("//x")` is relative to the **opened** .blend. In headless batches use absolute paths, or set them after `open_mainfile`.
- GPU in containers: Cycles CUDA/OptiX needs the NVIDIA container runtime. Otherwise use CPU. EEVEE needs a GPU/EGL even headless.

title: Pipeline Automation: CI recipe (GitHub Actions)
text:
## CI recipe (GitHub Actions)
Download the Linux tarball (`https://download.blender.org/release/Blender5.2/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64.tar.xz`), cache it, then `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P tests/run_all.py`. This repo's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a working example.

title: Rendering: One call
text:
# Rendering

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Scene lighting and cameras are in `blender-lighting-lookdev`.

## One call
```
scripts/render_batch.py -- --engine CYCLES --preset final --res 1920 1080 --out //render/hero_#### --frames 1
scripts/render_batch.py -- --preset preview --frames 1-120 --format MP4 --out //render/turntable
scripts/render_batch.py -- --cameras CamA CamB CamC --format EXR_MULTI --out //render/shots/
```
Presets: `preview` (Cycles 64 spp, threshold 0.05, 50% res; EEVEE 16), `final` (512 spp, 0.01; EEVEE 128 + raytracing), `product` (1024 spp, transparent background). GPU is picked automatically (OptiX > CUDA > HIP > Metal > oneAPI), and the denoiser matches (OptiX or OpenImageDenoise).

title: Rendering: Engine choice
text:
## Engine choice
| Engine | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cycles | final quality, product, archviz, glass/SSS/caustics, baking | path tracer; set the GPU; adaptive sampling + denoise |
| EEVEE (5.x, ex-"Next") | fast look-dev, stylized, motion graphics, previews | ray-traced reflections/GI (`use_raytracing`), virtual shadow maps; needs a GPU even headless |
| Workbench | playblasts, clay/matcap reviews, QA sheets | instant, no lighting accuracy |
Engine ids: `CYCLES`, `BLENDER_EEVEE`, `BLENDER_WORKBENCH`.

## Cycles quality levers (ordered by impact)
1. **Adaptive sampling** (`adaptive_threshold` 0.01 final / 0.05 preview) + **denoise** (OIDN with albedo+normal passes, `denoising_input_passes="RGB_ALBEDO_NORMAL"`). Raising samples alone is the least efficient fix.
2. **Light paths**: interiors need diffuse bounces ≥ 4. Product shots: total 12, glossy 4, transmission 8–12 for glass. Clamp indirect 5–10 kills fireflies at a small energy cost.
3. **Light tree** (`use_light_tree`, on) for many lights. **Path guiding** (CPU only) for difficult indirect light.
4. Fewer, larger lights beat many small ones. Emissive meshes are noisier than area lights.
5. Persistent data (`render.use_persistent_data`) speeds up animations and turntables. Use `simplify` (max subdivision, texture limit) for previews.
6. 5.2: **texture cache** (`render.use_texture_cache`, `use_auto_generate_texture_cache`) cuts memory in texture-heavy scenes by generating `.tx` mip tiles.

title: Rendering: Color management (decide once per project)
text:
## Color management (decide once per project)
- **AgX** (default): photographic, handles bright highlights. Looks: `AgX - Punchy`, `- Base Contrast`...
- **Khronos PBR Neutral**: shows albedo faithfully. Use it for product/e-commerce and asset reviews, and to match three.js `NeutralToneMapping`.
- **Standard**: graphics/UI/texture output that must match pixel values.
- **ACES 1.3 / 2.0**: VFX pipelines (plates, other DCCs).
- Use exposure (`view_settings.exposure`), not light power, for global brightness tweaks. Display device sRGB, or Display P3 / Rec.2100 for HDR delivery.

## Output formats
- Stills: PNG 8/16-bit (RGBA when the film is transparent) or JPEG for web previews.
- Comp/VFX: **EXR multilayer** (`EXR_MULTI`, DWAA 16-bit) with passes (Denoising Data, Cryptomatte, AO, Mist, Z). 5.0 renamed passes: `Diffuse Color`, `Depth`, etc.
- Video: render **frames first** (PNG/EXR), then encode (FFmpeg or the VSE), because a crash mid-MP4 loses everything. Direct MP4 is fine for previews. Set `image_settings.media_type` **before** `file_format` (5.0+).
- Transparent: `film_transparent=True` + PNG/EXR. A glass-only alpha needs `film_transparent_glass`.

title: Rendering: Compositor (5.0+ API)
text:
## Compositor (5.0+ API)
```python
ng = bpy.data.node_groups.new("Comp", "CompositorNodeTree"); scene.compositing_node_group = ng
ng.interface.new_socket("Image", in_out="OUTPUT", socket_type="NodeSocketColor")
rl, glare, out = ng.nodes.new("CompositorNodeRLayers"), ng.nodes.new("CompositorNodeGlare"), ng.nodes.new("NodeGroupOutput")
ng.links.new(rl.outputs["Image"], glare.inputs["Image"]); ng.links.new(glare.outputs["Image"], out.inputs[0])
```
There's no Composite node anymore: the group output is the final image. Many node options are now **input sockets** (Glare `Type`, `Threshold`, `Strength`), so `--describe` them with `blender-geometry-nodes/scripts/gn_builder.py`. File Output node: `directory`, `file_name`, `file_output_items`.

title: Rendering: CLI rendering (render farms, CI)
text:
## CLI rendering (render farms, CI)
- `blender -b scene.blend -E CYCLES -o //out/frame_#### -F PNG -s 1 -e 120 -a` renders an animation. `-f 10` renders a single frame. Python args go after `--`.
- `-- --cycles-device OPTIX` (or CUDA/HIP/METAL/ONEAPI) selects the device without Python.
- Split frames across machines with `-s/-e`, or with Placeholders + No Overwrite (`render.use_placeholder`, `use_overwrite=False`) on shared storage.

## Gotchas
- `scene.render.engine` enum under-reports (add-on engines). Assign in try/except (the script does).
- EEVEE in background still needs a GPU context. In CI without a GPU, use Cycles CPU or Workbench.
- `bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)` writes `render.filepath`. Without `write_still`, the result only lives in `Render Result`.
- Noise in glass/caustics: enable caustics only if needed (`caustics_refractive`), raise transmission bounces, or fake it with Thin Wall (5.2) for windows.
- Fireflies: clamp indirect, a filter glossy / blur glossy (`blur_glossy` 0.5–1), and bigger light sources.

title: Retopology & UVs: Retopology
text:
# Retopology & UVs

The execution model is in `blender-core`.

## Retopology
**Automatic** (`scripts/auto_retopo.py -- --objects Sculpt --tris 8000 --method ...`) makes `<name>_low` and leaves the source hidden:
| Method | Use for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `quadriflow` | organic props, static characters, scans | clean quads. Voxel-remeshes first so the input is manifold; UVs are lost (re-unwrap) |
| `decimate` | background props, LODs, AI-generated meshes | keeps UVs/shape, gives triangles. Fast |
| `planar` | hard-surface CAD/boolean results | dissolves flat areas; keeps seams/sharp/material/UV borders |

**Manual** (hero characters, anything that deforms). Set up a new mesh object with a Shrinkwrap modifier (`PROJECT`, target = sculpt), snapping to `FACE_PROJECT` + `use_snap_project`, and the source in a different viewport color/x-ray. Auto retopo isn't good enough for deforming hero meshes, because the edge flow below matters.

title: Retopology & UVs: Edge flow rules for deforming meshes
text:
### Edge flow rules for deforming meshes
- Concentric loops around the eyes and mouth (≥3 rings). The nasolabial loop flows from the nose wing to the mouth corner.
- **3 loops** at every bending joint (elbow, knee, finger knuckles), plus a loop on each side to keep volume. The shoulder needs extra loops for raising the arm.
- Keep poles (3/5-edge verts) out of bending areas. Put them on flat, stiff regions (chest, back of skull).
- Distribute quads evenly, with density where deformation and silhouette need it. Use triangles only in hidden, non-deforming spots.
- Character tri budgets in 2026: mobile 5–15k, Roblox body ≤ 10.7k total, console/PC third-person 30–80k, hero/cinematic 100k+. Check the target in `blender-game-optimization`.

title: Retopology & UVs: UVs
text:
## UVs
1. **Seams**: hide them (under arms, inner legs, back of the head, under parts), follow hard edges, cut cylinders on the back side. Rule for game meshes: every hard edge (>~60°, `sharp_edge`) **must** be a UV seam, or the normal map shows artifacts. `scripts/uv_pack.py --seams-from-sharp 60` does this.
2. **Unwrap**: `--method seams` (Angle Based with marked seams), `--method min_stretch` (SLIM, 4.3+, least distortion on organics), `--method smart` (hard-surface/auto, `--angle 66`).
3. **Straighten** rectangular islands (Follow Active Quads, live only) so trims and pixel grids line up.
4. **Average island scale + pack** with margin in pixels: 2k → 8 px, 4k → 16 px, mobile 1k → 4 px. `--shape CONCAVE` gives the tightest pack (slow headless). The default `AABB` is instant.
5. **Texel density** (`scripts/texel_density.py --res 2048`): keep `spread` ≤ 1.3 within an asset. Set it with `--set <px/m>`; if `fits_0_1` is false, change res or density.
6. QA: `blender-asset-qa` reports zero-area UV faces and overlap %.

title: Retopology & UVs: Texel density targets (px/m; studio baselines, not laws)
text:
### Texel density targets (px/m; studio baselines, not laws)
| Context | px/m |
|---|---|
| First-person hero / weapons | 1024–2048 |
| First-person environment | 512–1024 |
| Third-person games | 512 (console/PC), 256 (mobile) |
| Top-down / strategy | 128–256 |
| Roblox | ~256–512 per texture: 5×5 studs → 256², 10×10 → 512², 20×20 → 1024² |
Everything in the same scene should share one density. The exception is hero assets, kept within 2x.

## Special cases
- **Mirrored/stacked UVs** save space but break unique bakes. Move the duplicate islands exactly +1 U (outside 0–1) during baking, then move them back. Their normal maps must be mirror-safe (tangent space handles it in engines with MikkTSpace).
- **Lightmap UV2** (`--lightmap`, gives `UVMap_Lightmap`): no overlaps, every island inside 0–1, generous margin. Unreal/Unity can generate their own; ship one only if the engine pipeline wants it. Keep UV0 active for texturing.
- **UDIMs** (film/hero): islands in tiles 1001+ (U offset 1 per tile). Texture node image `source="TILED"`. Game engines mostly don't support UDIMs.
- **Trim sheets**: unwrap the strips, then scale/move the islands onto the trim rows (V positions from the trim layout). Islands may exceed 0–1 in U for tiling.
- **Roblox**: exactly one UV set, all inside 0–1. Overlaps are allowed.

title: Retopology & UVs: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- 5.0+: UV selection is shared across UV maps (`.uv_select_*` attributes). Old `BMLoopUV.select` code fails.
- `uv.*` operators run in Edit Mode and act on selected faces. Select everything first (scripts handle this).
- Headless `uv.pack_islands` with `CONCAVE`/`CONVEX` + rotation can take 2–25 s even on tiny meshes. Use `AABB` while iterating.
- Unwrap warning "failed to solve island": the island has no seams (closed shape). Add seams.
- Apply scale before measuring texel density, or the density reads wrong (the scripts use world space and already account for scale).

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Procedure
text:
# Scene Setup & Hygiene

The execution model and verification steps are in `blender-core`.

## Procedure
1. Run `scripts/scene_audit.py` (add `--fix purge scale paths` only on files you own). It reports units, unapplied/negative scale, default names, objects in the scene root, missing images, orphans and far-off origins.
2. Set units: Metric, Unit Scale **1.0**, Length meters. Keep 1.0 even for Unreal/Roblox, because exporters handle the conversion (see `blender-export-pipelines`).
3. Build the collection layout (below). Every object must be in a named collection, never the scene root.
4. Name everything with the conventions below. Rename after every duplicate or join so no `.001` suffixes remain.
5. Set origins: props at the bottom-center (they sit on the ground at Z=0), characters at world origin between the feet, doors/hinges at the pivot.
6. Apply rotation and scale on meshes (Ctrl+A). Keep location unless the asset should export at the origin.
7. Re-run the audit. It's done when `issues` is empty or every remaining issue is intentional and explained.

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Collection layout (one asset per .blend, or one collection per asset)
text:
## Collection layout (one asset per .blend, or one collection per asset)
```
ASSET_Crate
├── Crate_high      # sculpt / subdiv source (exclude from export)
├── Crate_low       # game mesh(es) SM_Crate, SM_Crate_LOD1..
├── Crate_bake      # cages, bake helpers
├── Crate_collision # UCX_SM_Crate_00 (UE) / Crate-col (Godot)
└── Crate_ref       # reference images/blockout (hide_render)
```
Use **Collection Exporters** (4.2+) to define the export once per collection, then re-export with one call:
```python
with bpy.context.temp_override(collection=col):
    bpy.ops.collection.exporter_add(name="IO_FH_gltf2")
ex = col.exporters[-1]; ex.export_properties.filepath = "//export/SM_Crate.glb"
with bpy.context.temp_override(collection=col):
    bpy.ops.collection.exporter_export(index=len(col.exporters) - 1)
```
`bpy.ops.wm.collection_export_all()` re-runs every collection exporter.

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Naming conventions (Unreal-style, accepted by all engines)
text:
## Naming conventions (Unreal-style, accepted by all engines)
| Type | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Static mesh | `SM_<Name>[_LOD#]` | `SM_Crate_LOD1` |
| Skeletal mesh / rig | `SK_<Name>` / `RIG_<Name>` (armature object `Armature` or `root`) | `SK_Hero` |
| Material | `M_<Name>` / instance `MI_<Name>` | `M_Wood_Oak` |
| Texture | `T_<Name>_<Suffix>`: `_BC` base color, `_N` normal, `_ORM` (R=AO G=Rough B=Metal), `_E` emissive, `_M` mask | `T_Crate_ORM` |
| Collision | UE `UCX_<Mesh>_##`, Godot suffix `-col`/`-colonly`/`-convcolonly` | `UCX_SM_Crate_00` |
| Bones/sides | `.L`/`.R` suffix (Blender mirror tools depend on it) | `upper_arm.L` |
| Actions | `<Rig>_<Clip>` | `Hero_Run` |
Use ASCII only, no spaces, and PascalCase or snake_case consistently across the project.

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Real-world scale reference (meters)
text:
## Real-world scale reference (meters)
Door 2.0–2.1 × 0.9 · ceiling 2.4–2.7 · table 0.75 · chair seat 0.45 · counter 0.9 · stair rise 0.18 / tread 0.28 · adult human 1.7–1.8 (eyes 1.6) · car 4.5 × 1.8 × 1.5. Roblox: 1 stud ≈ 0.28 m; default character ≈ 5 studs tall. Wrong scale breaks physics, lighting falloff, DOF and texel density, so check `ob.dimensions` first.

## Linking, appending, overrides
- **Append** (`libraries.load(link=False)`) makes a local copy. Use it for one-off reuse.
- **Link** (`link=True`) is read-only, updates from the source and is what pipelines use. To edit a linked collection, add a library override: `ob.override_hierarchy_create(scene, view_layer, do_fully_editable=False)`. Only overridable properties (transforms, pose, and anything marked overridable) can change.
- Keep library paths relative (`//`). Check `bpy.data.libraries` for broken paths.

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Asset libraries
text:
## Asset libraries
- Mark: `ob.asset_mark(); ob.asset_generate_preview()`. Metadata goes in `ob.asset_data` (`author`, `description`, `license`, `tags.new("wood")`, `catalog_id`).
- Catalogs live in `blender_assets.cats.txt` at the library root, one line per catalog: `UUID:Path/Sub:Simple Name`.
- Register a library with `prefs.filepaths.asset_libraries.new(name=..., directory=...)`. 5.2+: remote libraries via `use_remote_url` + `remote_url`. In 5.2 `active_asset_library` indices are offset by 2 ("All", "Essentials").
- Import method per library: `LINK`, `APPEND`, `APPEND_REUSE` (default; reuses already-appended data).

title: Scene Setup & Hygiene: Hygiene rules
text:
## Hygiene rules
- Purge orphans before shipping (`bpy.data.orphans_purge(do_recursive=True)`). Use fake users only on purpose.
- Image paths: relative (`file.make_paths_relative`), or pack for single-file delivery (`file.pack_all`).
- Never ship multi-user mesh data that has an unapplied per-object scale. Instances are fine, but bake scale before export.
- Hide helpers with `hide_render=True` **and** exclude them from export collections; viewport hiding alone isn't enough.
- One active scene per file for delivery. Extra scenes confuse exporters (`use_active_scene`).

title: Sculpting: Agents: what you can and can't do
text:
# Sculpting

The execution model is in `blender-core`. The handoff goes to `blender-retopology-uv` → `blender-texture-baking`.

## Agents: what you can and can't do
- **Sculpt Mode operators crash Blender in background mode** (`-b`), including `mesh_filter`. Never enter Sculpt Mode headless.
- Headless or MCP: use `scripts/sculpt_ops.py` for object-level ops: `remesh=SIZE`, `symmetrize=+X`, `multires=N`, `inflate=D`, `detail=STR,SCALE`, `smooth=N`, `apply`. Combine these with Geometry Nodes (`blender-geometry-nodes`: SDF grid booleans/fillets, noise displacement) and shape modeling for procedural organic forms.
- Live sessions with a UI: brush strokes via `bpy.ops.sculpt.brush_stroke(stroke=[...])` need a 3D View region override and are fragile. Prefer procedural ops, then show the user with `look`. Hand detailed brushwork to the human.

title: Sculpting: Professional workflow
text:
## Professional workflow
1. **Base mesh / blockout**: primitives, metaballs, Skin modifier, or a low-poly base at real scale. Proportions first: compare with references and check against a human 1.75 m.
2. **Unify**: voxel remesh (`remesh=0.02` for a 2 m character, smaller for detail) fuses parts and gives even density. Repeat it while the big forms change.
3. **Primary forms** at low resolution (Grab, Snake Hook, Clay Strips, Inflate, Smooth). **Secondary** (muscle groups, folds) at medium resolution. **Tertiary** (pores, scratches, fabric weave) with Multires levels 4–6, or as normal/displacement maps.
4. **Dynamic topology** (`sculpt.dynamic_topology_toggle`): adds detail where you stroke. Good for concept sculpting, bad for final topology and multires (it destroys UVs/multires). Use voxel remesh + multires for production.
5. **Multires**: subdivide (`multires_subdivide`, Catmull-Clark) on a clean quad base (after retopo) to sculpt high detail that bakes back to the base level (`blender-texture-baking`, multires bake or high→low).
6. **Handoff**: export the high (or keep it in-file), retopo to `_low`, UV, bake normal/AO/curvature, then texture.

title: Sculpting: Brushes (5.x: brushes are assets in the Essentials library)
text:
## Brushes (5.x: brushes are assets in the Essentials library)
| Purpose | `sculpt_brush_type` |
|---|---|
| Build volume | `CLAY_STRIPS`, `CLAY`, `CLAY_THUMB`, `LAYER`, `INFLATE`, `BLOB` |
| Shape / move | `GRAB`, `SNAKE_HOOK`, `ELASTIC_DEFORM`, `POSE`, `BOUNDARY`, `CLOTH`, `NUDGE`, `ROTATE`, `THUMB` |
| Details / edges | `DRAW`, `DRAW_SHARP`, `CREASE`, `PINCH` |
| Flatten / hard surface | `PLANE` (flatten/fill/scrape), `MULTIPLANE_SCRAPE` |
| Clean up | `SMOOTH`, `SIMPLIFY` (dyntopo), `DISPLACEMENT_ERASER`/`SMEAR` (multires) |
| Masking / grouping | `MASK`, `DRAW_FACE_SETS`; Expand (`sculpt.expand`), mask from cavity |
5.0 renamed `brush.sculpt_tool` → `sculpt_brush_type`. 5.1 folded the stroke options into `brush.stroke_method` (`DOTS`, `DRAG_DOT`, `SPACE`, `AIRBRUSH`, `ANCHORED`, `LINE`, `CURVE`). 5.2 moved automasking to `brush.mesh_automasking_settings` / `paint.mesh_automasking_settings`.

title: Sculpting: Rules of thumb
text:
## Rules of thumb
- Sculpt at **real scale**, with scale applied. Brush radius is in screen space but strength and remesh sizes depend on scale.
- Use symmetry (`mesh.use_mirror_x`, radial: `mesh.radial_symmetry`) on characters until the asymmetry pass at the end.
- Face Sets organise parts (head, torso, hands). Hide them and mask by face set to isolate.
- Watch density: a 2 m character at voxel 0.005 is already millions of polys. Keep viewport FPS usable and work up in levels.
- Silhouette first. Check from several angles in flat matcap (`look` shading `solid`) before adding detail.
- Floaters/kitbash for hard-surface details on organic models: separate objects, combined at bake time.
- Before baking, run `blender-asset-qa` on the high (no inverted parts, no huge self-intersections in the bake range).

title: Sculpting: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- `voxel_remesh` destroys UVs, vertex groups (unless preserve attributes) and multires levels. Do it before UVs/rigging.
- Multires + topology changes don't mix: never edit the base topology after subdividing (apply the base or rebuild).
- `symmetrize` on a non-centered object mirrors across the **object's local axis**. Center the origin on the symmetry plane first.
- Sculpting on shape keys: enable `use_shape_key_edit_mode` and sculpt on the active key (facial work, `blender-facial-shapekeys`).

title: Simulation: One call
text:
# Simulation

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Procedural sim zones are in `blender-geometry-nodes`.

## One call
```
scripts/sim_setup.py -- --rigid --active Crate1 Crate2 --passive Floor --density 500 --frames 1 120 --bake --to-keys
scripts/sim_setup.py -- --cloth Flag --preset cotton --pin Pin --colliders Pole --bake
scripts/sim_setup.py -- --gn-cloth Sheet --colliders Table --set Bendiness=0.5 Stretchiness=0.1 --bake
```
`--bake` steps through every frame in order (this works headless for point caches **and** GN simulation zones) and reports final positions and `min_z`, so you can verify contact. `--to-keys` turns rigid-body motion into keyframes for engines.

title: Simulation: Choose the solver
text:
## Choose the solver
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Falling/stacking/destruction | Rigid Body (Bullet). Pre-fracture with Cell Fracture (extension) or GN Voronoi |
| Clothing, flags, drapes (production-proven) | Classic **Cloth** modifier + Collision modifiers |
| New node-based cloth/hair, custom forces, procedural setups | **Cloth Dynamics (Experimental)** / **Hair Dynamics** assets (5.2, XPBD) |
| Liquids, smoke, fire | Mantaflow fluid domain + flow/effector (`fluid.bake_all`) |
| Hair grooms | Curves objects + hair node assets (`procedural_hair_node_assets`), Hair Dynamics for motion |
| Growth, trails, custom per-frame logic | GN Simulation zone |
| Soft jiggle for games | bones with spring/jiggle in-engine, or Wiggle-style constraints baked to keys |

title: Simulation: Rigid bodies
text:
## Rigid bodies
- Real scale and real mass matter: mass = volume × density (wood 500–700, concrete 2400, steel 7850, plastic 950 kg/m³). The script computes it.
- Collision shape: `CONVEX_HULL` for dynamic objects (fast, stable), `MESH` only for **passive** concave colliders, and primitives (`BOX`, `SPHERE`, `CAPSULE`) when they fit.
- Stability: substeps 10 and iterations 10 (set by the script). Use a small collision margin (1 mm). Avoid objects starting interpenetrated.
- Export: bake to keyframes (`--to-keys`; the built-in `rigidbody.bake_to_keyframes` needs a UI, so the script samples `matrix_world` itself), then export the actions (`blender-export-pipelines`).

title: Simulation: Classic cloth
text:
## Classic cloth
- Presets (from Blender's): cotton, denim, leather, rubber, silk. The mesh needs even quad density (2–5 cm edges for clothing). Use a subdivided plane or retopologized garment, never ngons.
- **Pinning**: vertex group with weight 1 = pinned (`settings.vertex_group_mass`). Animate pinned verts with hooks/armature.
- Collisions: colliders get a `COLLISION` modifier (thickness 1–5 mm), plus self-collision for folds. Raise `quality` (steps) for fast motion.
- Apply cloth as a shape (`modifier_apply_as_shapekey`) or bake to an Alembic/point cache for render. Games: bake to bones, or apply a static drape.

title: Simulation: Node-based dynamics (5.2, experimental)
text:
## Node-based dynamics (5.2, experimental)
- Assets live in `datafiles/assets/nodes/geometry_nodes_dynamics_assets.blend`: `Cloth Dynamics (Experimental)`, `Hair Dynamics`, `Collider`, `Set Effector`, `Custom Force`, `Custom Effector`. The script appends them.
- Cloth inputs include `Pin Group` (attribute), `Stretchiness`, `Bendiness`, `Substeps` (5), `Constraint Steps` (15), `Mass`, `Friction`, `Collision Radius`, `Linear Damping`, `Gravity`, `Tearing` (+ mode/threshold), `Effectors Collection`, `Effectors` (bundle).
- Colliders: put a `Collider` modifier on each collider object and add those objects to the collection fed into `Effectors Collection` (the script does both).
- Hair: Add → Empty Hair sets up the surface + `Capture Rest Geometry`. Hair Dynamics reads the rest/deformed surface through geometry bundles.
- Limits (5.2): no self-collision yet, no built-in wind/turbulence (build a `Custom Force`). Interfaces may change, so pin the Blender version in production.
- The solver itself (`GeometryNodeXPBDSolver`) takes a `World` bundle, `Delta Time`, `Substeps`, `Constraint Iterations`. Building directly on it is advanced; start from the assets.

title: Simulation: Fluids (Mantaflow) quick setup
text:
## Fluids (Mantaflow) quick setup
Domain object (`FLUID` modifier `fluid_type="DOMAIN"`, `domain_type="LIQUID"|"GAS"`), resolution 64 preview / 128–256 final, cache directory set and `cache_type="ALL"` for headless; flow objects `fluid_type="FLOW"` (`flow_type` LIQUID/SMOKE/FIRE, `flow_behavior` INFLOW/GEOMETRY); obstacles `EFFECTOR`. Bake with `bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()` under a context override with the domain active. This is slow. Test at low resolution first.

## Rules
- Simulations are frame-rate and scale dependent. Set `scene.render.fps` and the scale before tuning.
- Always bake before rendering/exporting, and never rely on viewport playback order.
- GN simulation zones: bake per modifier (`mod.bakes`, `object.geometry_node_bake_single`), or step frames sequentially (script) in background.
- Point caches in background: stepping frames from `frame_start` fills the cache. `ptcache.bake_all(bake=True)` needs a valid context.
- Verify with `look(mode="frames")` plus the numbers (`min_z` ≈ the collider top = contact, no tunnelling).

title: Simulation: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- Objects tunnelling through colliders: thin colliders, too few substeps, or too-fast motion. Thicken, raise substeps/quality, or use a bigger collision distance.
- Exploding cloth at frame 1: starting interpenetration or a zero-area face. Run `blender-asset-qa`, offset the start.
- Rigid body world cache ranges are separate from the scene range (the script syncs them).
- Changing anything (frame range, settings) invalidates caches. Re-bake.

title: Texture Baking (Cycles): One call
text:
# Texture Baking (Cycles)

The execution model is in `blender-core`. UVs come from `blender-retopology-uv` and materials from `blender-pbr-materials`.

## One call
```
scripts/bake_maps.py -- --low SM_Crate --high Crate_high Crate_bolts --maps normal ao curvature id \
   --res 2048 --samples 64 --margin-px 16 --pack-orm --out //textures
```
Self-bake (procedural → textures, no `--high`): `--low SM_Crate --maps basecolor roughness metallic normal --pack-orm`.
The script picks the GPU (OptiX/CUDA/HIP/Metal/oneAPI) and falls back to CPU, creates the target images with correct color spaces, cleans up its temporary nodes, and saves `T_<name>_<N|AO|CURV|BC|R|M|ORM...>.png`.

title: Texture Baking (Cycles): Preparation checklist (most bake bugs come from this list)
text:
## Preparation checklist (most bake bugs come from this list)
1. **Low poly**: UVs unwrapped, no overlaps (stacked/mirrored islands moved +1 U), padding ≥ 8 px at the bake resolution, scale applied.
2. **Hard edges = UV seams** on the low poly. Use either smooth shading with the bake handling gradients, or hard edges split at seams. Never put a hard edge inside a UV island.
3. **Triangulate the low poly the same way the engine will**, or export the triangulated mesh. Mismatched triangulation shows as shading seams.
4. **High poly** covers the low completely and pokes out of it only a little. Floaters (bolts, panel details) can hover just above the surface, but must stay within the extrusion distance.
5. **Names**: `X_low` / `X_high` pairs. Bake per part, or explode the parts apart (move each pair along an axis) so neighbouring parts don't project onto each other, then put them back.
6. Apply modifiers on the high poly as needed (multires and subd are evaluated automatically).

title: Texture Baking (Cycles): Rays: extrusion vs cage
text:
## Rays: extrusion vs cage
- `--extrusion` (meters) pushes the ray origin outward from the low surface. It must be **greater than the farthest distance the high poly sticks out** of the low. The default is 2% of the low's diagonal; `max_ray_distance` is 2 × extrusion.
- **Cage** (`--cage Crate_cage`): a copy of the low with the same topology, inflated (Displace/"Push"). Use it when uniform extrusion fails (sharp concave corners, thin parts). Edit the cage locally where rays miss.
- Too small: holes or missing details. Too large: other parts of the mesh project in (intersections, "ghosting").

## Map guide
| Map | Space | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| normal | Non-Color, tangent, OpenGL (`--directx` for Unreal) | 16-sample AA is plenty; 8-bit PNG is fine for games |
| ao | Non-Color | 64–256 samples; bake with the high only (no ground) unless contact AO is wanted |
| curvature | Non-Color, 0.5 = flat | derived from the baked normal (convex white / concave dark); drives edge wear |
| id | sRGB | one flat color per high-poly **material**; use materials as masks |
| thickness | Non-Color | AO with inside rays; dark = thin; for SSS/translucency masks |
| basecolor/metallic/opacity | via emission override | reads the Principled inputs of the source materials (also procedural chains) |
| roughness, emit, combined | native Cycles passes | combined = lit result (lightmaps, stylized) |
| position | float | gradient masks |
ORM = R:AO G:Roughness B:Metallic, the glTF/Unreal standard. Unity uses a different packing (`blender-pbr-materials`).

title: Texture Baking (Cycles): Fixing common artifacts
text:
## Fixing common artifacts
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Wavy lines on cylinders | low poly too low, smoothing gradients | add segments, use a cage, or more support on the low |
| Skewed details (bolts lean) | ray direction follows the averaged low normals | hard edges + seams, a cage, or bake the floater separately |
| Black/garbage areas | rays miss or hit the back faces | raise extrusion, fix flipped normals (`blender-asset-qa`), check high coverage |
| Seams visible in engine | margin too small, hard edge without a seam, different tangents | margin ≥ 16 px @2k, seams at hard edges, export tangents (MikkTSpace) |
| Details from a neighbouring part | parts too close | explode the bake, or bake per object pair |
| Inverted green look in engine | OpenGL/DirectX mismatch | `--directx` for Unreal, or flip G in the texture importer |
| Stepping/banding | 8-bit with large flat gradients | bake to 16-bit (`float_buffer`) and dither on export |

title: Texture Baking (Cycles): Baking non-PBR data
text:
## Baking non-PBR data
- **Vertex colors**: `bake.target = "VERTEX_COLORS"` with an active color attribute (useful for mobile and Roblox-free shading).
- **Lightmaps**: bake `combined` onto UV2 (`--uv-layer UVMap_Lightmap`) with the scene lights.
- **Multires** (no separate high object): `bake.use_multires=True`, `bake.type="NORMALS"|"DISPLACEMENT"|"VECTOR_DISPLACEMENT"`, `bake.use_lores_mesh=True`, then `bpy.ops.object.bake_image()`. The viewport level is the low, the sculpt level is the high.

## Gotchas
- The target image must be the **active** Image Texture node in **every** material of the low object (the script handles this).
- Baking in Cycles uses the active UV map (`--uv-layer` to pick).
- Images aren't saved automatically: `img.save()` or `save_render`. Packed or internal images disappear on reload.
- 5.2: the Cycles texture cache (`.tx`) is for render memory and doesn't affect bake results.
- Run `blender-asset-qa` on low + high first, because flipped normals and floating chunks produce most bake garbage.

title: Fog and volumetrics (5.2): Density from visibility
text:
# Fog and volumetrics (5.2)

## Density from visibility
Meteorological visibility V (m) is where contrast drops to 2%. Extinction σ = 3.912 / V (Koschmieder), in units of 1/m (Blender units = meters). For Principled Volume with a white `Color`, `Density` ≈ σ.

| V (m) | σ (Density) | Look |
|---|---|---|
| 10000 | 0.0004 | clear air, distant mountains fade |
| 2000 | 0.002 | haze |
| 500 | 0.008 | mist |
| 150 | 0.026 | fog |
| 40 | 0.098 | dense fog |
| 15 | 0.26 | can't see across the street |

**Height fog**: `density(z) = σ · exp(−(z − ground) / H)`, H = 1–3 m (ground fog) or 5–20 m (valley/city). `scene_mood.py --fog-height H` builds it with Geometry Position → Math nodes.

title: Fog and volumetrics (5.2): Phase function (forward scattering = glow around lights and god rays)
text:
## Phase function (forward scattering = glow around lights and god rays)
- Principled Volume `Anisotropy` 0.5–0.7 for fog and haze, 0.85 for water. 0 = isotropic, a flat look.
- Volume Scatter in 5.x has `phase`: `HENYEY_GREENSTEIN`, `FOURNIER_FORAND`, `DRAINE`, `RAYLEIGH`, `MIE`. `MIE` + `Diameter` (µm; fog droplets ~10–20) is the most physical choice for fog in Cycles. `RAYLEIGH` suits clear-air blue scattering. Principled Volume `Anisotropy` is the safe choice when a file must render in both engines.

## Cycles
- 5.0+: **null scattering** is the default (unbiased, handles mixed dense/thin volumes, no step size). `cycles.volume_biased = True` restores ray marching (`volume_step_rate`, `volume_max_steps`), which is sometimes faster for simple homogeneous fog.
- `cycles.volume_bounces` 0 = single scattering (fast, darker). 1–2 for dense, bright fog.
- Noise: volumes converge slowly. Use 256+ spp with adaptive sampling, the OIDN denoiser, and a **separate fog pass**: put the fog box in its own view layer, set the other objects to holdout, and composite. Fog denoises much better alone.
- `use_volume_guiding` (path guiding, CPU) helps dense lit fog.

title: Fog and volumetrics (5.2): EEVEE (5.x)
text:
## EEVEE (5.x)
- Froxel grid: `eevee.volumetric_tile_size` "2"/"4"/"8", `volumetric_samples` 64–128, and `volumetric_start/end`: the range must enclose the fog, and a tight range gives more precision.
- `use_volumetric_shadows` (+ `volumetric_shadow_samples`) is required for god rays.
- `volumetric_ray_depth` (accurate volume intersection) raises the count of overlapping volume surfaces you can stack before artifacts appear.
- World volumes are infinite in EEVEE; use a box for local fog. Thin slabs and very dense fog band, so use cards or Cycles for those.

## God rays checklist
Strong directional key → occluder with gaps (window frame, trees, slatted blinds) → fog σ 0.01–0.05 with anisotropy 0.6–0.8 → camera looking toward the light. Cycles gives crisp shafts. In EEVEE, enable volumetric shadows and use tile size 2.

title: Fog and volumetrics (5.2): Cheap alternatives
text:
## Cheap alternatives
- **Mist pass**: `view_layer.use_pass_mist`, `world.mist_settings` (`start`, `depth`, `falloff`). Mix the fog color in the compositor using the mist as the factor. No volume cost, but no light shafts.
- **Fog cards**: camera-facing planes with a soft alpha-noise emission/transparent material, for background layers. They intersect geometry visibly, so keep them clear of objects.

title: Light values (measured in Blender 5.2.2): Sun by elevation (Multiple Scattering sky, altitude 100 m, default air/aerosol/ozone)
text:
# Light values (measured in Blender 5.2.2)

## Sun by elevation (Multiple Scattering sky, altitude 100 m, default air/aerosol/ozone)
Sun color = normalized direct-normal irradiance. "Sun W/m²" is the lamp strength `scene_mood.py` uses before exposure balancing (sky strength 0.0285). "Sky share" = sky irradiance on a horizontal plane ÷ direct irradiance on a horizontal plane.

| Elevation | Name | Sun color (RGB) | Sun W/m² | Sky share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60° | noon | 1.00 0.86 0.68 | 4.0 | 0.12 |
| 35° | afternoon | 1.00 0.83 0.61 | 3.7 | 0.16 |
| 20° | morning | 1.00 0.78 0.49 | 3.2 | 0.26 |
| 6° | golden | 1.00 0.55 0.16 | 1.4 | 0.98 |
| 1° | sunrise/sunset | 1.00 0.22 0.00 | 0.19 | 17 |
| −4° | blue hour | (no direct sun) | 0 | sky only, strongly blue |
| < −12° | night | (sky ≈ black) | 0 | use the night dome + moon |

The sky goes from dominating at the horizon to about 12% of the light at noon. This is why golden hour shadows are blue and noon shadows are deep.

title: Light values (measured in Blender 5.2.2): Lamp units (measured: white Lambert plane, Cycles)
text:
## Lamp units (measured: white Lambert plane, Cycles)
| Lamp | Irradiance at distance r |
|---|---|
| Sun, strength S | E = S (W/m²) |
| Point / spot, power P | E = P / (4π r²) |
| Area (small, on axis), power P | E = P / (π r²) |
A grey card reads 0.18 when E ≈ π (≈ 3.14) at exposure 0.

## Color temperature of real sources
| Source | Kelvin |
|---|---|
| Candle / fire | 1800–1900 |
| High-pressure sodium street lamp | 2000–2200 |
| Tungsten bulb | 2700 |
| Warm LED / halogen | 3000 |
| Neutral LED street lamp / fluorescent | 4000–4500 |
| Moonlight (physical) | ~4100 (render it cooler: Purkinje shift) |
| Noon sun | 5500–5800 |
| Overcast sky | 6500–7500 |
| Blue-hour sky | 9000–12000 |
In 5.x: `light.use_temperature = True; light.temperature = 2700`. `light.color` still multiplies the temperature color.

title: Light values (measured in Blender 5.2.2): Practical wattages (exposure 0, the scene_mood balance)
text:
## Practical wattages (exposure 0, the scene_mood balance)
| Source | Blender light |
|---|---|
| Table lamp / 60 W bulb | point 30–60 W, radius 0.05 m |
| Street lamp | spot 200–600 W, 2000–4000 K, spot size 100–140° |
| Window glow (interior lit) | area light in the window or emission 2–10 |
| Neon tube | emission strength 5–30 on a tube mesh + a weak area light for the spill |
| Car headlight | spot 300–800 W, blend 0.3, 5000 K |
With `--use-exposure`, multiply by the returned `practical_scale`.

## Sky texture parameters
- `altitude` (m): higher = darker, bluer sky with less haze. `air_density` scales Rayleigh (blue). `aerosol_density` scales Mie (haze, whiter sky, a bigger glow around the sun). `ozone_density` deepens twilight blue.
- Hazy or polluted day: `aerosol_density` 2–5. Crisp mountain air: `altitude` 2000+, `aerosol_density` 0.3.
- Both scattering models are very bright by default (physical units), so keep them balanced with a sun lamp or exposure. Never crank the strength to 1 and leave it.

title: Night, blue hour and stylized moods: Night that reads as night
text:
# Night, blue hour and stylized moods

## Night that reads as night
1. **Contrast, not darkness**: one hard key (moon, high sun lamp angle ≈ 0.5°, crisp shadows) plus pools of warm practicals, with backgrounds falling to silhouette. A uniformly dim, blue image reads as underexposed day.
2. **Color split**: cool ambient/moon (`[0.72, 0.82, 1.0]` or 7000–9000 K) against warm practicals (2000–3000 K). The complementary contrast sells it.
3. **Lower saturation**: compositor Hue/Saturation 0.7–0.85. The eye loses color vision at night (Purkinje shift).
4. **Night sky**: night HDRIs often contain light pollution that ruins rural scenes, so use the procedural dome (`--city-glow 0` for wilderness). The moon disc is not rendered: put a textured plane far away, or use an HDRI with a moon, if it must be visible.
5. **Practicals first in a moonless scene**: windows, street lamps and signs carry the image. Add a little fog (`--fog-visibility 200–500`) so lights bloom and cast visible cones.
6. **Camera**: a real night exposure means a longer shutter (more motion blur), a wider aperture (shallower depth of field) and grain. Keep `render.motion_blur_shutter` at 0.5 or above for moving elements.
7. **Workflow**: turn lights on one at a time. A night scene with ten lights often works with three. Use light groups / light linking (`blender-lighting-lookdev`) to balance them without moving them.

title: Night, blue hour and stylized moods: Blue hour (sun 4–6° below the horizon)
text:
## Blue hour (sun 4–6° below the horizon)
- Sky-only lighting: soft and deep blue, with no shadows. The best moment is when the practicals balance the sky, not overpower it: the script's balance keeps 50 W lamps visible but not blown out.
- Windows and street lights on, a warm/cool split, a long exposure look (smooth water, light trails).

## Golden hour / sunset
- Sun 0–8°: warm key (measured `[1, 0.55, 0.16]` at 6°), long shadows, blue shadow fill from the sky.
- Backlight or rim the subject and let the sun flare (compositor Glare `Fog Glow` or `Streaks`, threshold 1).
- Haze adds depth: `--fog-visibility 2000–5000` with `--fog-color 1 0.85 0.7`.

title: Night, blue hour and stylized moods: Moods (`--mood`)
text:
## Moods (`--mood`)
| Mood | Time and key | Atmosphere | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| cyberpunk | moonless; magenta + cyan area rim pair | fog 150 m, 10 m height, magenta city glow | AgX - Punchy, bloom 0.6, saturation 1.1 |
| horror | night; low moon 12°, sickly cyan | fog 35 m hugging the ground (1.5 m) | AgX - High Contrast, saturation 0.55, darker |
| underwater | sun 70° through water | uniform volume 30 m, teal scatter, absorption tint | AgX - Base Contrast, saturation 0.9 |
| desert | sun 45°, hot | warm haze 3000 m | AgX - Medium High Contrast, warm white point |

### Finishing each mood
- **cyberpunk**: wet streets are half the look (`blender-weather-fx` `surface_weather.py --wetness 0.7 --puddles 0.5`). Add emissive neon signs (strength 10–30) with light-linked spill, and rain for drama.
- **horror**: one motivated source (a flickering bulb: keyframe the energy with noise), deep vignettes, fog between the camera and the subject, a desaturated green-cyan cast. Hide the threat in silhouette.
- **underwater**: caustics need either a gobo/projected texture or Cycles caustics, which are slow. The fast fake is an animated Voronoi caustic pattern (W or Mapping driven by `frame`) added as brightness in the ground's shader, or on a gobo plane in front of a spot light. Add floating particles (`precipitation.py --type dust`), god rays from the surface (anisotropy 0.85), and blur the background.
- **desert**: high sun, short shadows, bleached highlights. Add a heat shimmer in comp (`CompositorNodeDisplace` driven by a small animated noise) and dust particles in the air. Use high albedo sand (0.4–0.6 sRGB).

title: Night, blue hour and stylized moods: Grade order (compositor, 5.x API: options are input sockets)
text:
## Grade order (compositor, 5.x API: options are input sockets)
Render Layers → Glare (`Type` "Bloom" / "Fog Glow", `Threshold` 1, `Strength`) → Color Balance (`Type` "White Point", `Input Temperature`) → Hue/Saturation → (Lens Distortion `Dispersion` 0.01–0.03 for a stylized look) → Group Output. `scene.compositing_node_group` holds the tree.

title: Time of Day & Atmosphere: One call
text:
# Time of Day & Atmosphere

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Studio and product lighting are in `blender-lighting-lookdev`, render settings in `blender-rendering`, and rain, snow, wetness and lightning in `blender-weather-fx`.

## One call
```
scripts/scene_mood.py -- --time golden                       # sun 6 deg, warm, long shadows
scripts/scene_mood.py -- --time night --fog-visibility 250   # moonlight + stars + haze
scripts/scene_mood.py -- --time noon --overcast 0.8          # soft grey day
scripts/scene_mood.py -- --mood cyberpunk                    # moonless, neon rim pair, fog, bloom
scripts/scene_mood.py -- --time morning --fog-visibility 120 --fog-height 4   # valley fog
```
Times: `noon morning afternoon golden sunrise sunset blue_hour night moonless`. Moods: `cyberpunk horror underwater desert` (each sets defaults that explicit flags override). Override the sun with `--elevation DEG` (negative = below the horizon) and `--heading DEG` (0 = +Y, 90 = +X). If you leave out `--heading`, the sun sits 135° from the camera's view direction, which gives side/back light that shows form. Front light looks flat.

The script builds `ENV_World`, the `ENV_Mood` collection (sun or moon, fog box, accent lights) and, for moods, `ENV_Grade` (a compositor tree). Your objects are untouched, and re-running replaces everything it made. It returns the key light's strength, color and elevation, the exposure, and any warnings.

title: Time of Day & Atmosphere: How it stays physically right
text:
## How it stays physically right
- **Sky**: `ShaderNodeTexSky` `MULTIPLE_SCATTERING` (5.0+; `SINGLE_SCATTERING` is the legacy "Nishita") with `sun_disc=False`. A **Sun lamp** is the sun, because it gives sharp shadows in both engines. The lamp's color and its strength relative to the sky come from a table **measured from Blender 5.2's own sky model** at each elevation (sunset sun ≈ `[1.0, 0.22, 0]`, noon ≈ `[1.0, 0.86, 0.68]`). That keeps the sky and the sun consistent.
- **Scale**: noon gives a sun of ≈ 4 W/m² with a grey card at 0.18 under AgX at exposure 0.
- **Exposure balance**: each preset meters a grey card between the ground and a wall facing the sun, then scales the *environment* lights so the card lands at the preset's brightness (noon 1.0, golden 0.85, sunset 0.7, blue hour 0.35, night 0.2, moonless 0.1). Your practical lights keep their usual wattage and read correctly against it.
- **Physical alternative**: `--use-exposure` puts the difference in `view_settings.exposure` instead. The result returns `practical_scale`: multiply your lamp wattages by it to keep the same look.
- **Night**: the moon is a Sun lamp at 0.3 W/m² before scaling (35°, cool `[0.72, 0.82, 1.0]`; moonlight is physically ~4100 K, and it reads blue because of the Purkinje shift). The night dome is a zenith gradient, a city glow at the horizon (sodium orange; magenta for cyberpunk), and stars visible to camera rays only.
- **Fog**: a box volume around the scene and the camera. Density = **3.912 / visibility** (Koschmieder: visibility in meters → extinction per meter). Add `--fog-height` for an exponential ground fog. Exposure compensates for light lost in fog by up to 4 EV, so fog stays dense instead of just dark. The background seen by the camera is blended toward the fog color.

title: Time of Day & Atmosphere: Fog and volumetrics
text:
## Fog and volumetrics
| Look | `--fog-visibility` (m) |
|---|---|
| Clear air / distant haze | 5000–20000 |
| Haze, desert dust | 1000–3000 |
| Mist | 500–1000 |
| Fog | 100–500 |
| Dense fog, horror | 20–60 |
| Underwater (clear → murky) | 30 → 8 |
- **God rays** need four things: a strong key (sun/spot), occluders (windows, trees, a gobo), forward scattering (`--fog-anisotropy 0.6–0.85`), and EEVEE `use_volumetric_shadows` (the script turns it on).
- **Cycles 5.x** renders volumes with **null scattering** by default (unbiased, no step size). `scene.cycles.volume_biased=True` brings back ray marching (`volume_step_rate`). Height fog is a heterogeneous volume and is noisier, so give it more samples or denoise.
- **EEVEE** volumes are froxels: `volumetric_tile_size` 4 → 2 for detail, and `volumetric_end` must cover the fog (the script sets it). Very dense fog close to the camera bands, so prefer Cycles for it.
- Cheap distant haze without volumes: the Mist pass (`view_layer.use_pass_mist`, `world.mist_settings.start/depth`) mixed in the compositor.
- Deeper detail is in [references/fog-volumetrics.md](references/fog-volumetrics.md).

title: Time of Day & Atmosphere: Rules
text:
## Rules
- Decide the light direction first (side/back), then the time. Low sun (golden, sunset) = long shadows and warm key against a cool sky fill, which is the most flattering combination.
- Night is not "a blue tint": keep **contrast** (hard moon shadows, pools of warm practicals, dark silhouettes), lower saturation, and add practical sources. See [references/night-and-moods.md](references/night-and-moods.md).
- Practicals use real color temperatures (`light.use_temperature=True`, `light.temperature`): sodium 2000 K, tungsten 2700 K, warm LED 3000 K, neutral LED 4000 K, neon as emissive tubes. Watts and conversions are in [references/light-values.md](references/light-values.md).
- Keep the view transform AgX (the script sets it, along with a mood look like `AgX - Punchy`). `--keep-view` preserves yours.
- Verify every mood with a render, not the viewport: fog, stars and bloom only show in rendered output. Use `blender-rendering` `render_batch.py --preset preview`.

title: Time of Day & Atmosphere: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- Below the horizon the sky texture shows a dark "ground". Extend the ground plane or terrain to the horizon, or keep the horizon out of frame.
- The bloom/glare threshold is **scene-linear, before** the view exposure. With `--use-exposure` the script scales the threshold for you.
- The script won't overwrite a compositor tree that isn't `ENV_Grade`; it reports that instead.
- `SunLight.use_nodes` and light node trees are deprecated in 5.x (removal planned for 6.0). Use light color and `temperature` instead.
- The sky texture's `sun_direction` only applies to the legacy Preetham/Hosek models. `sun_rotation` 0 places the sun toward +Y and 90° toward +X (measured).
- Changing the render engine doesn't need a re-run. The script sets both the EEVEE and Cycles volume settings.

title: Weather for games and real-time: What to export from Blender
text:
# Weather for games and real-time

In engines, weather is a runtime system: particles, post-processing and material parameters. Blender's job is to deliver **meshes and masks** that the engine shaders read. Never export rain or snow instances as geometry.

## What to export from Blender
| Asset | How |
|---|---|
| Wetness/puddle/snow mask per vertex | `surface_weather.py --vertex-mask` → color attribute `ENV_Weather` (R puddles, G snow, B walls). Make it the active color attribute (`mesh.color_attributes.active_color_name = "ENV_Weather"`) |
| Mask textures | bake the wet material with `blender-texture-baking` (self-bake: basecolor/roughness), or bake the mask into a channel of a packed texture |
| Snow cover mesh | apply `ENV_SnowCover` (or export it as a separate LOD-able mesh), then `blender-asset-qa` + `blender-game-optimization` |
| Puddle decals | planes with a water material, slightly above the ground (≥ 2 mm, never coplanar: z-fighting) |
| Rain splash / ripple flipbooks | render a top-down ripple with `surface_weather` on a plane (orthographic camera), then pack the frames into an atlas |

Exporter flags (5.2): glTF `export_vertex_color="ACTIVE"` (or `"NAME"` + `export_vertex_color_name="ENV_Weather"`); FBX `colors_type="LINEAR"` for masks (sRGB would gamma-shift the values) with `prioritize_active_color=True`.

title: Weather for games and real-time: Engine side (what reads the masks)
text:
## Engine side (what reads the masks)
- **Unreal**: a wetness material function (darken albedo, lower roughness, puddle normal flatten), driven by a Material Parameter Collection `Wetness` × vertex color R. Rain = Niagara GPU sprites with depth-buffer collision, plus ripple decals.
- **Unity (URP/HDRP)**: a Shader Graph wet layer using vertex color, or HDRP decals for puddles. Rain = VFX Graph (GPU) with depth collision. Snow = a vertex color G blend to a snow layer.
- **Godot 4**: a ShaderMaterial reading `COLOR`, with GPUParticles3D + a particle collision heightfield.
- **Roblox**: no custom shaders. Use MaterialVariant / SurfaceAppearance swaps for wet and snowy versions, ParticleEmitter (`Speed`, `Acceleration`, `Drag`) for rain and snow, and Atmosphere (`Density`, `Haze`, `Glare`) for fog. Keep particle `Rate` low on mobile.

title: Weather for games and real-time: Budgets
text:
## Budgets
- Rain on mobile: around a few hundred camera-attached sprites. PC/console: thousands of GPU particles. Never use per-drop geometry.
- Masks: vertex colors cost nothing extra if the mesh already has colors. A mask texture shares an existing packed channel (for example the A of ORM).
- Fog: engine height fog (Unreal Exponential Height Fog, Unity Fog, Roblox Atmosphere). Match its density to `scene_mood` visibility: extinction ≈ 3.912 / visibility (m).

title: Weather values and look library: Rain
text:
# Weather values and look library

## Rain
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Terminal velocity by drop diameter | 0.5 mm ≈ 2 m/s · 1 mm ≈ 4 · 2 mm ≈ 6.5 · 5 mm ≈ 9 m/s (Gunn & Kinzer) |
| Rain rate classes | light < 2.5 mm/h · moderate 2.5–7.6 · heavy > 7.6 (AMS) |
| On camera | a streak = speed × exposure time: 7 m/s × 1/48 s ≈ 15 cm at 24 fps with a 180° shutter |
| Splash | crown 2–4 cm, lives ~50–100 ms; secondary droplets bounce 5–10 cm |
| Water | IOR 1.33, roughness 0–0.05 still, 0.05–0.15 rippled |
- Visible density is far lower than physical density (thousands of tiny drops per m³). `precipitation.py` uses 5–80/m³ of *visible* streaks; storms read better with fog and wind than with more particles.
- Wind tilts the rain: 2–5 m/s for a slant, 10+ for a storm. Gusts: keyframe the modifier's `Wind` input.
- Rain is lit by what's behind it. Rim and backlight it (street lamps, headlights, a bright sky). Against a bright sky it reads dark; against a dark background it reads bright.

title: Weather values and look library: Wet surfaces (after Lagarde, "Water drop" series)
text:
## Wet surfaces (after Lagarde, "Water drop" series)
- Porous materials (asphalt, concrete, brick, wood, fabric) darken by 20–50% as water fills the pores. Non-porous ones (metal, glass, plastic, car paint) don't darken, they only gain a water film.
- Wet roughness drops sharply. Puddles are mirrors (water film ≈ 0.02) and hide the underlying normal detail (`surface_weather.py` flattens the base normal under puddles).
- Puddles collect in low, flat areas: up-facing faces and cavities. To place them yourself, paint a vertex color or mask and feed it to the group's `Puddles` input.
- Drying edges: a thin darker rim around puddles (the wet halo) sells it. Widen the mask edge if needed.

title: Weather values and look library: Snow
text:
## Snow
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Fall speed | flakes 0.5–1.5 m/s, graupel 1–3 m/s |
| Flake size | 2–10 mm (big wet flakes up to 2–5 cm in calm air) |
| Albedo | fresh 0.8–0.9 · old/settled 0.6–0.8 · melting/dirty 0.4–0.6 |
| Look | strong subsurface (blue-shifted radius), roughness 0.5–0.7, sparkle = tiny glossy flakes |
- Snow settles on surfaces facing up, thins at edges, and is absent under overhangs. The shader handles facing; occlusion needs a painted mask or a raycast/AO bake.
- Real thickness (`--snow-depth`) matters on roofs, ledges and the ground. Thin dustings stay shader-only.

title: Weather values and look library: Dust, ash, embers
text:
## Dust, ash, embers
- Dust: tiny (0.5–1 mm), slow, floating (sway). Visible only in beams of light, so pair it with fog + god rays.
- Ash: flat flakes, slow tumbling fall, dark grey; post-fire or volcanic mood.
- Embers: emissive orange (strength 10–50), rising and swaying, short-lived. Pair with bloom (`scene_mood.py` grade) and a warm point light near the fire.

## Lightning
- A flash is 3–4 return strokes ~40–60 ms apart, 0.2–0.5 s total; the bolt channel shows a bright core with glow.
- Cloud-to-ground bolts start at the cloud base (1–3 km up). Branches fork downward.
- The flash lights the scene from the strike direction with cool white light (≈ 8000 K), stronger than the moon.
- Use 1–3 flashes per shot. Constant flashing reads as a strobe, not a storm.

title: Weather FX: One call each
text:
# Weather FX

The execution model is in `blender-core`. Sky, sun/moon, fog and mood come from `blender-time-of-day`, so run `scene_mood.py` first, then add weather. Rendering settings are in `blender-rendering`.

## One call each
```
scripts/precipitation.py -- --type rain --intensity heavy --ground Street Roofs --wind 2 0
scripts/surface_weather.py -- --objects Street Car Walls --wetness 0.7 --puddles 0.4 --ripples 1 --streaks 0.5
scripts/lightning.py -- --flashes 2 --strokes 3
scripts/precipitation.py -- --type snow --intensity moderate --ground Terrain
scripts/surface_weather.py -- --objects Terrain Roofs --snow 0.8 --snow-depth 0.06
scripts/surface_weather.py -- --objects Street Car Walls --remove     # exact restore
```
A rainy night: `scene_mood.py --time night --fog-visibility 250` → rain → wetness + puddles → lightning. Rain and puddles at night are what sell a wet scene: wet surfaces reflect every practical light.

title: Weather FX: precipitation.py (rain, snow, dust, ash, embers)
text:
## precipitation.py (rain, snow, dust, ash, embers)
- Builds a GN modifier on `ENV_Weather_<Type>`. Its box covers what the camera sees across the frame range: world-fixed, so moving cameras don't drag the rain. With no camera, it covers a 18 m box. The floor is the lowest top of `--ground`.
- **Seamless loop with no simulation**: each particle lives N whole times per loop (`Lives`), so the last frame + 1 equals the first frame exactly. It renders any frame on its own and works headless.
- **Real speeds**: rain 7 m/s (9 at heavy/storm), snow 1, ash 0.6, dust 0.15, embers rise at 1.5, combined with `--wind X Y` (m/s).
- **Ground**: a raycast against the `--ground` objects stops particles at the first hit (roofs, awnings, streets). Rain spawns splash crowns lasting 80 ms at each hit, aligned to the surface normal.
- **Streaks, not motion blur**: rain is a 3-sided streak of length = speed × ½ frame (a 180° shutter), aligned to the travel direction. Motion blur off is cheaper and looks the same.
- Particles closer than 1.5 m to the camera are hidden (`Near Clear`), because huge blobs ruin shots. The viewport shows 10% (`Viewport Fraction`), renders show 100%.
- Density per intensity (particles/m³): rain 5/15/40/80, snow 10/30/80/160. Override with `--density`. The count is capped by `--max-count` (400k), and the result warns when it caps.
- All values remain modifier inputs (Count, Speed, Wind, Lives, Particle Size, Streak Length, Sway, Ground, Splash...), so tweak them there instead of re-running.

title: Weather FX: surface_weather.py (wet, puddles, ripples, streaks, snow)
text:
## surface_weather.py (wet, puddles, ripples, streaks, snow)
- Puts one `ENV_Weather` shader group in front of each Principled BSDF and records the originals on the material. `--remove` restores links and values exactly.
- **Wet** (Lagarde model): porous albedo darkens (up to 55% × `--porosity`), roughness drops, and a water film is added as **Coat**. Use porosity 0.6–0.9 for asphalt, concrete, wood and fabric, and 0.1–0.2 for metal, glass and plastic.
- **Puddles**: domain-warped world-space noise on up-facing faces. Coverage ≈ `--puddles`, feature size `--scale` (m, default 3). Inside a puddle: full coat, mirror coat roughness 0.02, and a flattened base normal, because water fills the cracks.
- **Ripples**: expanding rings, one per ~17 cm cell, driven by a `frame` driver (a simple expression, so it works without auto-run scripts). They only show inside puddles.
- **Streaks**: vertical noise on walls adds coat runs.
- **Snow**: up-facing coverage with a noisy edge, albedo 0.9, roughness 0.6 and a fine bump. `--snow-depth` adds real thickness with the `ENV_SnowCover` GN modifier: up-facing faces are subdivided and extruded upward by a noise height that is never zero, so there's no z-fighting. It uses the `ENV_M_Snow` material with subsurface.
- `--vertex-mask` writes the `ENV_Weather` color attribute (R puddles, G snow, B walls) for engine shaders.

title: Weather FX: lightning.py
text:
## lightning.py
- A strike is 3 return strokes ~50 ms apart (at least 2 frames apart, so the flicker reads at 24 fps), each a peak followed by a 2-frame decay. `--strokes`, `--flashes` or `--frames` set the timing. The flash is a cool `ENV_Storm_Flash` sun (12° soft) keyed against the scene's key light (×2.5).
- `ENV_Storm_Bolt` is a branching emissive curve (midpoint displacement plus 4 branches), keyed with the flash. By default it is 300 m away, in frame and off-center. The world background strength flashes too (`--no-sky` to skip).
- Keys use LINEAR interpolation (flashes must snap, not ease).

title: Weather FX: Rules
text:
## Rules
- **Rain is visible only when backlit or side-lit** against a darker background: put a practical or bright sky behind it. Front-lit rain disappears.
- Combine layers: fog (atmosphere) + rain streaks (mid) + splashes/ripples (ground) + wet reflections. Any one alone looks fake.
- Real scale is mandatory: speeds, densities and puddle sizes are in meters (`blender-scene-setup`).
- Check with a render at the final resolution. Rain density and streak visibility don't show in the viewport (10% count, no fog).
- Run `blender-asset-qa` on the snow geometry if the asset will be exported.

## Games and real-time
Weather is an engine system (Unreal Niagara, Unity VFX Graph, Roblox ParticleEmitter). From Blender, export the **masks**: the vertex color attribute (`--vertex-mask`) or baked textures (`blender-texture-baking` self-bake of the wet material), plus snow cover meshes. Details are in [references/realtime-engines.md](references/realtime-engines.md). Physical values and the look library are in [references/weather-values.md](references/weather-values.md).

title: Weather FX: Gotchas
text:
## Gotchas
- GN particles are instances, so `object.data` stays empty. Read results through the evaluated depsgraph (`depsgraph.object_instances`).
- Background (`-b`) evaluation counts as the viewport for the `Is Viewport` node, so a headless test sees 10% of the count. Renders get 100%.
- Ground objects are linked into the `ENV_Weather_<Type>_Ground` collection (linked, not moved).
- `surface_weather` changes shared materials: every object using that material gets wet. Duplicate materials first to limit it.
- Coat appears in both engines. EEVEE needs raytracing on (`eevee.use_raytracing`) for good puddle reflections.

title: Workflow Recipes: 1. Game prop, mid-poly (fast, no bake)
text:
# Workflow Recipes

`S` = the skills folder. Every `.py` runs headless via `python S/blender-core/scripts/run_in_blender.py --blend F.blend S/<skill>/scripts/<x>.py -- ...`, or live via MCP import + `run()` (see `blender-core`). **Gate** = stop and fix before continuing. Save after every stage (`--save`).

## 1. Game prop, mid-poly (fast, no bake)
1. Blockout at real scale (`blender-hardsurface-modeling`). Gate: `ob.dimensions` vs reference.
2. UV the blockout **before** beveling (the Bevel/Boolean modifiers carry UVs): `uv_pack.py --objects SM_X --method seams --seams-from-sharp 60` → `texel_density.py --res 2048 --set 512`
3. `apply_stack.py --objects SM_X --preset midpoly [--cutters ...]` (keep it live; `--apply --triangulate` only on the export copy)
4. Materials: `build_pbr_material.py --preset ...` or tiling/trim textures.
5. Gate: `qa_check.py --objects SM_X --profile game` passes, plus `look` (angles, material + wireframe).
6. `mesh_stats.py --budget <platform>` → `make_lods.py --objects SM_X --rename`
7. `export_asset.py --preset <engine> --objects SM_X_LOD0 SM_X_LOD1 ...` Gate: re-import dims / GLB summary.

title: Workflow Recipes: 2. Game prop, high → low baked (hero quality)
text:
## 2. Game prop, high → low baked (hero quality)
1. High poly: hardsurface `--preset subd` or sculpt (`sculpt_ops.py`), named `X_high`.
2. Low: `auto_retopo.py --objects X_high --tris N --method planar|decimate|quadriflow`, or manual. Rename it `SM_X`.
3. `uv_pack.py --objects SM_X --method seams --seams-from-sharp 60 --margin-px 16`
4. Gate: `qa_check.py` on `SM_X` (game) **and** `X_high` (render profile, no inverted parts).
5. `bake_maps.py --low SM_X --high X_high --maps normal ao curvature id --pack-orm [--directx for Unreal]`
6. `build_pbr_material.py --name M_X --textures //textures --objects SM_X` (+ basecolor/roughness from texturing).
7. Gate: `look` in material shading (no seams/waviness), then steps 6–7 of recipe 1.

title: Workflow Recipes: 3. Game character (sculpt or AI mesh → animated export)
text:
## 3. Game character (sculpt or AI mesh → animated export)
1. Source mesh (sculpt / `generate_3d` / scan) at real height, facing -Y, feet on Z=0. Run `qa_check.py --profile render`.
2. `auto_retopo.py --method quadriflow --tris 20000` (or manual retopo for heroes, keeping the edge flow rules). `uv_pack.py --method min_stretch`.
3. `bake_maps.py --low Body --high Body_src --maps normal ao basecolor` (basecolor via emission override if the source has colors/materials).
4. `rigify_build.py --add basic_human --fit Body` → place joints (look xray) → `--metarig META_Body --generate`
5. `bind_mesh.py --armature RIG_Body --meshes Body` → `stress_poses.py --armature RIG_Body` → `look(mode="frames")`. Gate: no collapse at the elbows/knees/shoulders. Fix weights.
6. `rigify_build.py --rig RIG_Body --game-skeleton` → `rig_check.py --armature GAME_RIG_Body --profile unity|unreal`
7. Animate on RIG_Body (`blender-animation`) → `bake_action.py --source RIG_Body --target GAME_RIG_Body [--root-motion xy --hips spine]`
8. `export_asset.py --preset unity_skeletal|unreal_skeletal --objects GAME_RIG_Body` (meshes are included as children). Gate: GLB/FBX summary shows skins + all clips. Engine scale check.

title: Workflow Recipes: 4. Roblox
text:
## 4. Roblox
- **MeshPart prop**: recipe 1 with `--profile roblox` in QA (≤20k tris, watertight, no n-gons, single UV 0–1), separate grayscale maps (no ORM), `export_asset.py --preset roblox` (FBX) or `roblox_gltf`. Textures 1024² (PBR).
- **Rigid accessory**: ≤4k tris, an attachment point empty matching an R15 `_Att` name, `--preset roblox`.
- **Layered clothing**: start from Roblox's official cage templates. Build `<Name>_InnerCage`/`_OuterCage` (never change cage vertex count/order/UVs), skin to R15 bones, ≤4 influences, no weights on Root. Validate in Studio's Accessory Fitting Tool.
- **Avatar body**: 15 `_Geo` parts, R15 skeleton, attachments, outer cages, 10,742 tri budget. Read `blender-export-pipelines/references/roblox.md` first.
- Upload: Studio `AssetService:CreateAssetAsync` for batches.

title: Workflow Recipes: 5. Cleaning AI-generated / downloaded assets
text:
## 5. Cleaning AI-generated / downloaded assets
1. Import (`import_asset` / `generate_3d` / file). Scale to real size (`world_bounding_box`), origin to the bottom, ground at z=0, `transform_apply`.
2. `scene_audit.py --fix purge scale` → `qa_check.py --profile game`. Typical findings: non-manifold, duplicate verts, inverted islands, floating debris, z-fighting shells.
3. Fix: `make_lods.py --cleanup` (merge/degenerate/loose), recalc normals, delete floating debris (or `remesh` via `sculpt_ops.py` for garbage topology), then `auto_retopo.py --method decimate` to budget.
4. Re-UV if the UVs are fragmented (`uv_pack.py`) and re-bake from the original (`bake_maps.py --high original`).
5. Gate: QA passes + `look`. Never ship generated meshes unreviewed.

title: Workflow Recipes: 6. Procedural environment
text:
## 6. Procedural environment
1. Terrain/ground mesh, then a scatter tree with `gn_builder.py --spec scatter.json --apply Ground --set Density=... Seed=...` (recipes in `blender-geometry-nodes/references/recipes.md`).
2. Assets to scatter: optimized props with LODs (recipe 1). Keep instances (don't realize) for engines that support instancing (`export_gpu_instances`).
3. Gate: `mesh_stats.py` on the evaluated result, plus `look` from the gameplay camera height.

## 7. Web / AR asset
Recipe 1 or 2 with budgets `--budget web` (≤30k tris, 1–2 materials, 2k textures) → `export_asset.py --preset web` (meshopt + WebP) → optional `gltf-transform optimize --texture-compress ktx2`. USDZ for iOS AR: `--preset usd --out x.usdz`. Gate: GLB summary (size < 5 MB) and Khronos PBR Neutral look-dev match.

title: Workflow Recipes: 8. Product shot / turntable
text:
## 8. Product shot / turntable
1. Materials with measured values (`build_pbr_material.py --preset`), and QA for z-fighting/floating parts (very visible in close-ups).
2. Set the render resolution, then `turntable.py --objects Product --rig studio --backdrop --frames 120 --lens 85`
3. `render_batch.py --preset preview --frames 1` → review → `--preset product --frames 1-120 --format PNG` → encode, or `--format MP4`.
4. Gate: no fireflies or clipped highlights (AgX / Khronos PBR Neutral), and the product sits on the backdrop (contact shadow).

## 9. Mood / weather shot (rainy night, snowy morning, foggy dawn)
1. Scene at real scale with a camera. QA the hero assets first (wet reflections and snow expose z-fighting and gaps).
2. `scene_mood.py --time night --fog-visibility 250` (or `--mood cyberpunk|horror|underwater|desert`). Add practical lights (street, windows, neon) at real color temperatures.
3. Weather: `precipitation.py --type rain --intensity heavy --ground <ground/roofs>` → `surface_weather.py --objects <surfaces> --wetness 0.7 --puddles 0.4 --ripples 1 --streaks 0.5` → `lightning.py --flashes 2`. Snow: `--type snow` + `--snow 0.8 --snow-depth 0.06`.
4. Gate: `render_batch.py --preset preview --frames <mid>,<flash>` at the final aspect ratio. Rain must read (backlit), puddles must reflect a light, the night must keep contrast. Then render the full loop (frame range = the precipitation loop).
